articles.title: Los Rams, al frente, pero con dudas
articles.standfirst: Para William Hill sigue siendo el equipo favorito para ganar la Super Bowl
articles.summary: Para William Hill sigue siendo el equipo favorito para ganar la Super Bowl
articles.body: La primera semana de la NFL ya dejó su primera gran sacudida en las quinielas de cara al Super Bowl LXI en las casas de apuestas. Aunque no todo se ha movido tanto como podría parecer. Pese a caer de forma dolorosa ante San Francisco, Los Angeles Rams siguen siendo los favoritos del mercado, ahora a una cuota de 6.5 en William Hill. El equipo de Sean McVay llegó a Melbourne con todo el hype del verano y se marchó del Melbourne Cricket Ground goleado 27-7, superado en las tres fases del juego. Matthew Stafford apenas pudo mover la ofensiva ante una defensa dirigida por Kyle Shanahan que interceptó al quarterback angelino y asfixió a Puka Nacua. Es una derrota que duele, pero una sola jornada no borra el prestigio acumulado, y las casas de apuestas siguen viendo a los Rams como el equipo a batir. Justo detrás aparecen dos equipos que sí convencieron con la pelota en la mano: Buffalo Bills y Baltimore Ravens, ambos a cuota 10. Los Bills firmaron un auténtico festival ofensivo en Houston, imponiéndose 36-31 a los Texans en un partido de ida y vuelta en el que Josh Allen volvió a mostrar por qué sigue siendo el motor de su equipo, sumando otro touchdown de carrera a su ya extensa cuenta histórica. Del otro lado, los Ravens golearon 41-23 a los Colts en Indianápolis con una demostración de poderío total. 506 yardas de ataque, un Lamar Jackson sobrado de confianza tras superar sus problemas físicos y un Derrick Henry que a sus 32 años sigue rompiendo récords sobre la marcha. A continuación, a cuota 11 en William Hill, se sitúan los vigentes campeones, Seattle Seahawks. Los de Mike Macdonald protagonizaron un duelo apretado y con mucho morbo ante los New England Patriots, replicando de manera casi calcada la última final de la liga. Ganaron 13-10 en un partido que se decidió en el último cuarto, cuando Drake Maye se desmoronó con tres intercepciones consecutivas que Seattle supo aprovechar. No fue el partido más vistoso de la semana, pero sí uno con la épica justa para recordar por qué este equipo sigue llevando el anillo, incluso teniendo que recurrir a su suplente en el puesto de quarterback tras la lesión de Sam Darnold en la primera posesión. Cierran el quinteto de favoritos los San Francisco 49ers, a cuota 13, tras la que fue sin duda una de las imágenes más sólidas del arranque de temporada. Más allá del resultado ante los Rams, lo que dejó buenas sensaciones en las oficinas de Santa Clara fue la profundidad del plantel: Brock Purdy repartió tres pases de touchdown, Mike Evans debutó con gol en su primer partido de rojo y oro, y una defensa que dejó a Stafford completando apenas cuatro pases en la primera mitad. Si el nivel se sostiene, los 49ers tienen argumentos de sobra para escalar posiciones en las próximas semanas. Con solo una jornada disputada, el mercado de las apuestas deportivas sigue premiando la trayectoria por encima del resultado puntual, pero el margen para sorpresas ya está sobre la mesa. Las próximas semanas dirán si Rams, Bills, Ravens, Seahawks y 49ers mantienen su lugar en la conversación por el título o si el orden de favoritos empieza a reescribirse antes de lo previsto.

articles.title: Northwestern, HC David Braun Strike Long-Term Deal: 'He's Everything We Need'
articles.summary: The Northwestern Wildcats announced an extension with head coach David Braun.
articles.body: The Northwestern Wildcats are staying the course for years to come. Northwestern announced on Thursday morning that it has extended head coach David Braun to a deal that keeps him in place through the 2031 college football season. "David Braun is the right leader today for Northwestern Football and for the years to come," Combe Family Vice President for Athletics and Recreation Mark Jackson said in a statement on Thursday morning about the extension. "He recruits young men of high character who embrace our elite academic environment and who compete in the most competitive conference in the country. David develops our student-athletes at a time when retaining talent has never been harder, and they choose to remain Wildcats when other options appear. He does it with a rare combination of relentless competitiveness and integrity. "He is everything that we need in a head coach. With our continued investments in our Football program and with the opening of New Ryan Field in just a few weeks, the future of Northwestern Football is bright with David at the helm. We look forward to having David, Kristin and their family in Evanston for the seasons ahead." Braun originally joined Northwestern as its defensive coordinator for the 2023 season but was promoted to interim head coach in July of that year in the wake of head coach Pat Fitzgerald's dismissal against the backdrop of a hazing investigation into the program. After a 1-11 season in 2022, Northwestern went 8-5 overall and 5-4 in Big Ten play in Braun's first season at the helm, capped off by defeating the Utah Utes in the Las Vegas Bowl. Braun won 2023 Big Ten Coach of the Year honors and was named the Wildcats' full-time head coach during the season. The eight wins, which included Northwestern snapping a 14-game road losing streak, were the most for the Wildcats since finishing 10-3 overall and 7-2 in conference play in 2017. Since taking over in 2023, Northwestern is a combined 20-19 overall, 11-16 in Big Ten play and has made two bowl games under Braun (2023 and 2025). "I am so honored to have the opportunity to lead a storied football program at an institution that demands and expects excellence, instills character, and provides a transformative experience for its student-athletes on and off the field," Braun said in a statement about the extension. "I am grateful to President Chiang and to Mark Jackson for the continued investment into our program, for their support of my family and our tremendous staff and for sharing in our belief of what Northwestern Football can become. "Northwestern is a special place. Kristin and I are proud to call it home for many years to come." Prior to landing in Evanston in 2023, Braun was the defensive coordinator and safeties coach of the North Dakota State Bison from 2019-22, a stint preceded by two years as a defensive assistant with the Northern Iowa Panthers (2017-18), among other coaching positions. As for the present, Northwestern opened the 2026 season with a 34-18 win at home over the South Dakota State Jackrabbits on Sept. 5. Next up for the Wildcats is a Saturday night home matchup against the Colorado Buffaloes (2-0) at 7:30 p.m. ET, which can be viewed on FOX.

articles.title: El emotivo regreso de James al fútbol colombiano: debut, asistencia agónica y un sentido mensaje
articles.standfirst: James Rodríguez habla de su regreso a Atlético Nacional tras su brillante comienzo
articles.summary: James Rodríguez habla de su regreso a Atlético Nacional tras su brillante comienzo
articles.body: Casi dos décadas después de su partida al exterior, James Rodríguez volvió a jugar un partido oficial en la primera división del Fútbol Profesional Colombiano vistiendo la camiseta de Atlético Nacional. Tras su sonado fichaje por el conjunto verdolaga y la confirmación de su retiro de la Selección Colombia, el zurdo de 35 años protagonizó un debut de ensueño en Bogotá que culminó con un emotivo mensaje en sus redes sociales. El esperado estreno de James con la dorsal 23 de Atlético Nacional tuvo lugar en el Estadio Nemesio Camacho El Campín de Bogotá, ante una multitud de aficionados que abarrotaron las tribunas en el encuentro adelantado de la fecha 13 de la Liga BetPlay frente a Internacional de Bogotá. Al minuto 59, el técnico Lucas González dio paso al cucuteño en reemplazo de Juan Manuel Rengifo. El compromiso marchaba con un electrizante 2-2 tras los goles de Ian Poveda y Elías Cabrera para Nacional, y las anotaciones de Diego Duarte y Yojan "Pápula" Garcés para el cuadro local. Y en el minuto 90+9, cuando el empate parecía sentenciado, James ejecutó un preciso tiro de esquina al área que fue conectado de cabeza por Juan Manuel Zapata para sellar la victoria 2-3 a favor del cuadro antioqueño, con la primera asistencia del '10' vestido de verdolaga. Tuvieron que pasar 6.866 días (casi 19 años) desde la última vez que James Rodríguez disputó un partido de clubes en territorio colombiano. Curiosamente, su último juego en el país había sido en la final del torneo de ascenso con Envigado FC frente a Academia Compensar, disputada también en la capital colombiana. "Muy feliz de volver a jugar en mi país después de tanto tiempo. Gracias a la hinchada por el cariño y el recibimiento. Este triunfo es de todos y vamos por más", expresó el volante mediante una publicación acompañada de un video emotivo en sus redes oficiales. Tras el pitazo final, el director técnico de Atlético Nacional, Lucas González, elogió la jerarquía y el impacto de la llegada del astro colombiano al plantel: "El legado de James difícilmente se va a igualar en los próximos 50 años. Su calidad técnica y liderazgo dentro del grupo se notaron inmediatamente desde que pisó la cancha", señaló el estratega en rueda de prensa. Con este triunfo agónico, Atlético Nacional se consolida en la tabla de posiciones de la Liga BetPlay y se prepara para recibir a su afición en el Estadio Atanasio Girardot en las próximas jornadas.

articles.title: Lionel Messi Points Finger At MLS Commissioner Don Garber After Campeones Cup Final
articles.summary: Lionel Messi pointed his finger at MLS commissioner Don Garber on multiple occasions while speaking with him after Inter Miami’s game with Cruz Azul on Wednesday.
articles.body: Lionel Messi pointed his finger at MLS commissioner Don Garber on multiple occasions while speaking with him after Inter Miami’s game with Cruz Azul on Wednesday. Postgame video showed Messi pointing at Garber and speaking to him before walking away. He then appears later in the video pointing at him and talking to him again. Another video showed them pointing at each other as they spoke. MLS declined comment on the matter. Inter Miami didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment. The exchange came after Inter Miami defeated Cruz Azul 2-0 to win the Campeones Cup. Messi scored the 100th goal of his Inter Miami career during the game. This victory gave Inter Miami another trophy three years after Messi’s arrival. Miami won the Leagues Cup in 2023, the Supporters’ Shield in 2024 and MLS Cup in 2025. Reporting by The Associated Press.

articles.title: Who Is Drew Lock? 5 Things To Know About Seahawks QB Starting For Sam Darnold
articles.summary: With Sam Darnold injured, the Seahawks are starting Drew Lock at QB against the Cardinals. Here are five things to know about Lock.
articles.body: Lock it in! The Seattle Seahawks are putting 29-year-old quarterback Drew Lock under center for their Week 2 road matchup against the NFC West-rival Arizona Cardinals (Sunday afternoon at 4:25 p.m. ET on FOX), as starter Sam Darnold nurses a glute injury that he sustained in their Week 1 win over the New England Patriots. Here are five things to know about Lock: Drew Lock Starred At Missouri Drew Lock balled out for the Missouri Tigers. Serving as the Tigers' starting quarterback from 2016-18 — and being part of the program from 2015-18 — Lock averaged 3,620.3 passing yards, 31.7 passing touchdowns, 10.3 interceptions and a 148.7 passer rating per season over that span, while completing 58.4% of his passes. Most notably, Lock led the SEC with 3,964 passing yards, 44 passing touchdowns and a 165.7 passer rating in 2017. Granted, he also led the conference with 13 interceptions. Missouri appeared in a bowl game with Lock in both 2017 and 2018. Lock is second in Missouri history with 12,193 passing yards and 99 passing touchdowns. Drew Lock Was Part Of Broncos' QB Carousel In between Peyton Manning's final season (2015) and Russell Wilson's first season with the franchise (2022) — we'll revisit this shortly — 11 different players started at quarterback for the Denver Broncos. Lock was one of those 11 players. Denver selected Lock with the No. 42 pick in the 2019 NFL Draft, with him starting a combined 21 games from 2019-21. Lock was the team's primary quarterback in 2020, throwing for 2,933 yards, 16 touchdowns and 15 interceptions across 13 starts, while posting a 75.4 passer rating and completing 57.3% of his passes. He also rushed for 160 yards and three touchdowns. So, why did Denver's 2019 second-round pick only play three seasons for the team? Drew Lock Was In The Russell Wilson Blockbuster Lock was part of one of the biggest trades in NFL history. In March 2022, the Broncos traded Lock, tight end Noah Fant, defensive lineman Shelby Harris, two first-round picks, two-second round picks and a fifth-rounder to the Seahawks for star quarterback and then-nine-time Pro Bowler Russell Wilson and a fourth-round pick. Drew Lock's Consequential Career Game The New York Giants entered their Week 17 home tilt against the Indianapolis Colts with the worst record in the NFL and two losses away from having the No. 1 pick in the 2025 NFL Draft. Not on Lock's watch. After spending the bulk of the 2024 season as the team's backup to Daniel Jones, Lock made five starts after New York released Jones following a 2-8 start, with Lock's fourth start being arguably the best of his career and one of the best in Giants' history. In what was a 45-33 win for the Giants, Lock threw for 309 yards, four touchdowns and zero interceptions, while posting a career-high 155.3 passer rating – it was the third-highest passer rating in a game in Giants' history – completing 73.9% of his passes (17 of 23) and rushing for a score. The Giants went on to pick third in the 2025 NFL Draft. That said, one could argue it worked out for New York, which selected Penn State Nittany Lions linebacker Abdul Carter with the No. 3 pick and traded up to select Ole Miss Rebels quarterback Jaxson Dart with the No. 25 pick. Dart and the Giants opened the 2026 season with a win at home over the Dallas Cowboys, with the second-year quarterback throwing for 230 yards and three touchdowns, posting a 134.2 passer rating and completing 79.3% of his passes (23 of 29) in the victory. This Is Drew Lock's 2nd Stint In Seattle Of course, Lock landing in Seattle in 2022 and later playing one season for the Giants makes his presence with the Seahawks in 2026 his second act with the franchise. Act 1 got off to a bumpy start for Lock, who lost a quarterback battle to Geno Smith in 2022, with Smith going on to be the team's starting quarterback from 2022-24. With that said, Lock made two starts for the Seahawks in 2023, highlighted by hitting wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba for a go-ahead and eventual game-winning 29-yard touchdown pass with 28 seconds remaining in the fourth quarter of a Week 15 game against the Philadelphia Eagles on Monday Night Football. As for the present, Lock played all but the opening series in Seattle's Week 1 win over New England, throwing for 187 yards, one touchdown and no interceptions, while posting a 113.3 passer rating and completing 72.7% of his passes (16 of 22). Last year, Lock appeared in five regular-season games and one playoff game for the Seahawks, but he never made a start. Sunday will mark Lock's 29th NFL start.

articles.title: Dodgers Clinch 5th Straight NL West Title, Making It 13 In Past 14 Seasons
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Dodgers clinched their fifth consecutive NL West division title and 13th in the 14 seasons.
articles.body: The Los Angeles Dodgers clinched their fifth consecutive NL West division title and 13th in 14 seasons, sparked by four hits from Kyle Tucker that included a first-inning home run in an 8-2 win over the Cincinnati Reds on Thursday, The two-time World Series champions already were assured of their 14th straight postseason appearance, trying the record Atlanta set from 1991 to 2005. Los Angeles (93-60) had clinched no worse than a wild-card berth on Monday. Los Angeles opened a 9 1/2-game lead over second-place San Diego and has the second-best record in the NL as they try to overtake Milwaukee (95-57 entering Thursday) for the top NL seed. The division clinching was the fourth earliest for the Dodgers after Sept. 10 in 2019, Sept. 13 in 2022 and Sept. 16 in 2023. Tucker fell a triple short of the cycle and had three RBIs, hitting a single and a pair of doubles. He hit his 16th homer, a two-run drive in the first off Brady Singer, who allowed seven runs, nine hits and four walks in 3 1/3 innings. Freddie Freeman's sacrifice fly and Tucker's RBI double boosted the lead in the second, and the Dodgers opened a 7-0 lead in the fourth on Max Muncy's two-run double and Josue De Paula's RBI single. Dodger left-hander Justin Wrobleski, making his 22nd start this season and first since Sept. 6, did not allow a baserunner in three innings while striking out three. Wrobleski and Blake Treinen combined to retire their first 11 batters before Sal Stewart's 32nd homer. Landon Knack (1-0) allowed four hits over four scoreless innings for his first big league win since May 31 last year. Miguel Rojas homered off Brandon Williamson in the ninth. Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said reliever Edwin Diaz (neck inflammation) finished his minor league injury rehabilitation assignment and will be activated this weekend. Up next Dodgers: RHP Tyler Glasnow (4-1, 3.50) starts Friday against San Francisco, who send LHP Cesar Perdomo (0-1, 3.68) to the mound, Reds: RHP Chase Burns (15-3, 2.80) starts Friday against the Chicago Cubs.

articles.title: Should you start Bucs RB's this week in fantasy football?
articles.summary: Bucky Irving and Kenny Gainwell both have fantasy value entering the Bucs' Week 2 matchup against the Cleveland Browns.
articles.body:
The Buccaneers didn't lean heavily on the running game in their Week 1 loss to Cincinnati, but Bucky Irving still found a way to put together a productive fantasy performance. Now Tampa Bay returns home against Cleveland, with Kenny Gainwell and Sean Tucker also factoring into the fantasy conversation.

FantasyPros has Irving ranked as the RB18 for Week 2, while Gainwell comes in at RB37. Here's how I would handle all three Bucs running backs this week.

Irving didn't receive a massive workload against Cincinnati, but he made the most of it. He carried the ball eight times for 45 yards and a touchdown while catching seven passes for another 48 yards, giving him 93 total yards on 15 touches.

The seven receptions are what really stand out for fantasy purposes in PPR leagues. Irving doesn't necessarily need 20 carries to produce if Baker Mayfield continues looking his way in the passing game, especially in PPR formats.

FantasyPros projects Irving for 13.0 points and has him at RB18 this week. I'm comfortable starting him as an RB2 against Cleveland, and his involvement in both parts of the offense gives him a solid floor even if the Bucs continue splitting some of the backfield work. Also, if the game goes in the Bucs ' favor early and they get up by a few scores, Irving could see more carries as the game progresses.

Gainwell's Week 1 numbers weren't impressive at all. He finished with five carries for 15 yards and caught his only target for three yards, giving him just 18 yards from scrimmage. I'm still not ready to move away from him after one game.

FantasyPros has Gainwell at RB37 with an 8.7-point projection against Cleveland. That's firmly in the range where fantasy managers have to start making lineup decisions, and I'm willing to give him another shot as a flex option this week.

It's simply too early to completely give up on the role after one game. Week 2 should give us a much better idea of how Tampa Bay plans to divide this backfield. If Gainwell's opportunities don't increase and Irving once again handles most of the work on the ground and through the air, then Week 3 becomes a different conversation. For now, Gainwell is still someone I'm willing to use at flex.

Tucker is the one Bucs running back I'm keeping out of fantasy lineups this week. He missed the opener, so we haven't seen what his role will look like alongside Irving and Gainwell in a regular-season game yet.

That's enough uncertainty for me to keep him on the bench. There could eventually be a role for Tucker in this backfield, which would more than likely be goal-line carries and in short-yardage situations, but I'm not putting him into a Week 2 fantasy lineup before seeing how Tampa Bay actually uses him.

For this week, Irving is an easy start as an RB2, while I'm giving Gainwell another opportunity at flex. Tucker stays on the bench until we get a clearer picture of how the Bucs plan to divide the work.

articles.title: Georgia football has 5 players out for SEC opener vs. Arkansas
articles.summary: The Georgia Bulldogs are expected to be without five players for Week 3's game against the Arkansas Razorbacks
articles.body:
The Georgia Bulldogs finally have an official availability report heading into Week 3's game against the Arkansas Razorbacks . Georgia has three players listed on the availability report. However, the Bulldogs have five total players expected to miss the SEC opener.

Georgia linebacker Chase Linton missed the Bulldogs' first two games with a lower leg injury. Linton remains out and is considered "week-to-week" by Georgia coach Kirby Smart.

Georgia freshman cornerback Justice Fitzpatrick is recovering from a torn ACL (suffered in December) and is not back to 100%. Fitzpatrick remains out for the foreseeable future.

Georgia defensive lineman Xzavier McLeod is not with the team anymore . The Bulldogs will also be without Auburn Tigers transfer edge rusher Amaris Williams , who tore his ACL in the spring and is expected to miss the majority of the season at a minimum.

Williams and Kentucky Wildcats running back transfer Dante Dowdell are both not on Georgia's availability report, but will not play. Dowdell recently revealed he sustained a punctured lung, broken ribs, two broken collarbones and nerve damage to his right arm. He required nine staples in his head and was hospitalized for more than two months after getting in an ATV accident this offseason. Dowdell will be out for a long time.

The Bulldogs play Arkansas on Sept. 19 at noon ET. The temperature at kickoff will be around 90 degrees, which should test the depth and conditioning of both teams. Georgia and Arkansas will release an updated injury report 90 minutes before kickoff.

Out: Running back Dante Dowdell (upper body)

Out: Linebacker Amaris Williams (torn ACL)

Out: Linebacker Chase Linton (lower leg)

Questionable: Defensive back Brandon Ford

articles.title: Sean Payton says Davis Webb, Broncos will learn from Monday's game
articles.summary: "You learn from that," Broncos coach Sean Payton said after Davis Webb's play-calling debut. " "It's a quick turnaround."
articles.body:
After the Denver Broncos ' offense struggled in Week 1, many fans directed their ire at new offensive coordinator and play-caller Davis Webb , who made his regular-season debut in that role in a 31-10 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs .

The Broncos , however, have come to the defense of their young play-caller.

Denver quarterback Bo Nix said the offense let Webb down with a " pretty pitiful " performance. Nix argued that Webb had a good plan, but players failed to execute it.

Following the team's first practice of the week on Thursday, head coach Sean Payton said it was a poor performance across the board when asked about Webb.

"Listen, that game didn't go [well] for any of us as we would have hoped, right?" Payton said . "I said in the meeting this morning, there was dirt on a ton of people's hands, starting with me. So you learn from that. It's a quick turnaround."

After totaling just 176 net yards in their season opener, the Broncos' offense will attempt to bounce back against a Jacksonville Jaguars defense that allowed 272 net yards to the lowly Cleveland Browns in Week 1. If Denver's offense doesn't get back on track this week, Webb's status — at least among fans — will continue to be questioned.

articles.title: High stakes, social media barbs remind college football fans that Auburn and Florida share history of hatred
articles.summary: Auburn and Florida renew their 84-game rivalry as new head coaches Alex Golesh and Jon Sumrall face off in their first SEC game Saturday night.
articles.body: The center of the college football universe this coming weekend will undoubtedly be in Oxford, Mississippi, and it's easy to see why. Ole Miss and LSU are both top-ten teams with College Football Playoff and national title aspirations, but there's also the added bonus of former Rebels coach Lane Kiffin making his return to Vaught Hemingway Stadium for the first time as the new head coach of the Tigers. With all that in mind, there is a different game set to kick off around the same time in a different part of the SEC that will feature both extremely entertaining football and two fanbases with a ton at stake as well as plenty of hatred to go around. OLE MISS AND LSU WILL DELIVER CINEMA, BUT THE NEXT WEEK FOR EACH TEAM COULD BE THEIR MOST PIVOTAL TESTS In case you didn't know, Auburn and Florida are old rivals. I'm talking very old rivals. Before their annual matchups and bitter back-and-forth contests with LSU and Tennessee, the Gators considered the Tigers one of their biggest rivals, and the feeling was mutual on the other side. These two programs have met 84 times dating all the way back to 1912, and from 1945 until 2002, they played each other every year. Auburn holds the all-time series lead at 43-39-2, but the Gators have dominated the rivalry since 1990 when Steve Spurrier arrived in Gainesville, boasting a 12-6 record in that timeframe. That's not to say the Tigers haven't ruined plenty of Florida's best seasons in that stretch, and as a Gator fan coming of age during those years, I can speak to several personal experiences. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! I was a bit too young to remember 1994, when the Tigers marched into Ben Hill Griffin Stadium as 17.5-point underdogs and handed the top-ranked Gators their first and only regular season loss that year. I do, however, remember the 2006 Auburn team pouncing all over the second-ranked Gators to give that team their only loss en route to a national championship. The very next year, a reeling 2-2 Auburn squad upset top-five Florida in The Swamp, giving then-head coach Urban Meyer his first home loss as a Gator. That might explain part of why the rhetoric around this renewed rivalry is so toxic on social media this week, but it doesn't tell the whole story. History is only half of the equation here, as both the Tigers and Gators are breaking in new coaches who just as easily could have been on opposite sidelines. Saturday night will be the first SEC game for both Auburn head coach Alex Golesh and Florida head coach Jon Sumrall, so this contest will be a huge early test for two programs desperate to get off on the right foot in conference play. COLLEGE FOOTBALL’S CHAOS ERA IS HERE: TEXAS RALLIES, OREGON FALLS AND LANE KIFFIN EYES RETURN TO OLE MISS While the winner won't necessarily be out of the woods when it comes to proving they are ahead of schedule in year one, the loser will almost certainly be faced with some tough questions after failing to beat a team that is in a similar boat from a timeline perspective. There's also the added animosity Tigers fans likely feel towards Sumrall, who, by all accounts, was Auburn's top choice in their search for a new coach last November before he pivoted to the Gators. It's highly likely that both programs ended up with the best coach for them moving forward - I personally think Golesh will be great at Auburn and I'm obviously super high on Sumrall so far at Florida - but on Saturday night, Tiger fans will be eager to prove that the man who spurned them for a different shade of orange and blue made the wrong choice. Losing this game is going to suck for whichever coach, program, and fanbase fails to come out on top, and that's why it's so intriguing despite the fact neither team is ranked in the top-25. There are plenty of football-related aspects that make this matchup a must-watch, too, though. The chess match between Florida's offensive coordinator extraordinaire, Buster Faulkner, and Auburn's defensive coordinator DJ Durkin, who many consider one of the best in the conference, as well as the prospect of Gator running back Jadan Baugh going against the Tigers' stellar linebacker duo of Elijah Melendez and Xavier Atkins, will have football fans salivating. When you combine the off-field narratives with the on-field action, Auburn and Florida should provide one of the most entertaining matchups of the early season. articles.title: Richard Hughes' Liverpool gamble is already starting to look strange
articles.summary: Liverpool made a fair few signings in the summer. Four of them stayed at Anfield and have had a huge impact on Andoni Iraola's first season in charge so far....
articles.body:
Liverpool made a fair few signings in the summer.

Four of them stayed at Anfield and have had a huge impact on Andoni Iraola 's first season in charge so far.

However, two of them were sent out on loan to gain more experience.

Indeed, this has been the way things have been handled at Liverpool for a while now with the club always looking for ways to set themselves up for the future.

But, as with every club, some deals always feel a little bit strange and, after some fresh quotes have just emerged, one of Richard Hughes' final Liverpool gambles now looks a tad weird.

KRC Genk's director says he never expected Lucca Brughmans' transfer fee to be so high

Each of them have taken up a regular place in the Reds' starting XI with Araujo and Jacquet having the biggest impact so far.

However, as the summer transfer window edged closer to its deadline, there were a couple of last minute deals that the Anfield outfit managed to pull off.

These moves saw Lucca Brughmans and Djylian N'Guessan get snapped up by Liverpool and, while there was talk of Brughmans coming in as Liverpool's second-choice 'keeper, that never came to fruition.

Instead, he was loaned back to KRC Genk and now, in quotes relayed by Sports Witness, their sporting director, Dimitri de Conde shared how shocked he was about the fee Liverpool paid for the 18-year-old.

"I knew he was on the radar of top clubs," he said .

"He was one of the lads we hoped to get a handsome fee for at some point, to ensure the club's survival. But for it to happen that quickly. And for that amount, I never saw that coming.

"People saying 'It's fantastic what De Conde achieved with his experience regarding Lucca's transfer!' Sorry, but that's not the case.

"In the end, I got a call from his agency at 11am on a Sunday, two days before the English transfer window closed.

"Liverpool is serious. 'This is the offer.' And the very next morning, Lucca was on a plane to Liverpool. I do take credit for the fact that we, as a club, chose that path."

Liverpool could have paid less for Lucca Brughmans

When the price of Brughmans' deal was shared , fans were shocked.

Liverpool spent slightly more on the 18-year-old Belgian than they did on Giorgi Mamardashvili a couple of seasons ago which, with how much more experience the Georgian had over the Genk shot-stopper, is mind-boggling.

Obviously, Brughmans' potential needs to be taken into account but, even then, the transfer fee paid for the 18-year-old seems a tad excessive.

If he'd have come in as Liverpool's second-choice this season, there would have been so much pressure on his shoulders.

So, the fact that he's staying with Genk for at least another year is good news.

These quotes emerging do, however, make you question why on earth Hughes spent that much money on him at all.

Of course, his recent performances have proven how good he can actually be but, at the moment, it still remains to be seen whether or not he's going to be able to live up to expectations.

articles.title: Ex-Spurs star Gareth Bale speaks out on Tottenham's struggles and Roberto De Zerbi
articles.summary: Former Tottenham Hotspur star Gareth Bale has shared his thoughts on Spurs' difficult start to the Premier League season, whilst backing Roberto De Zerbi and...
articles.body:
Gareth Bale believes expectations at Tottenham Hotspur "need to be lowered a bit" this season following a rough start to the campaign.

Roberto De Zerbi's side, who avoided relegation to the EFL Championship on the final day last season following a hard-fought 1-0 home win against Everton , have failed to find the back of the net in their opening four top-flight games.

They scored five times in the Carabao Cup second round against Charlton Athletic but were knocked out of the competition on Tuesday following a 3-1 loss at Liverpool .

Nevertheless, Bale remains optimistic that the team will eventually find their rhythm, telling Sky Sports, via football.london : "Yeah, I think so [asked if Tottenham will be okay]. A lot of new signings. Sometimes it takes time to settle in.

"The manager has shown he is capable of playing good football. I think he still has the trust of everybody. There are a lot of new signings which takes a lot of time and I'm sure they will give him some time."

The former Tottenham winger - now retired - was then asked whether Spurs can still secure a European spot, to which he responded: "Hopefully, I think the expectation probably needs to be lowered a little bit considering we finished 17th twice in a row.

"I think an improvement was needed and obviously they've got the players to do that. Let's hope they gel soon and get going."

Tottenham welcome Aston Villa , who managed their first win of the season on Wednesday with a 3-1 victory at Coventry City, on Saturday as both sides pursue their maiden Premier League victory.

De Zerbi is calling for greater clinical efficiency from his squad in attacking areas, remarking following the defeat at Anfield: "We have to shoot more times, we have to shoot better, we have to finish better the clear situations, but we are sorry for the result, disappointed, frustrated for the result.

"I think, unfair, but we have to accept and to be stronger than this unlucky moment, because I'm honest, I'm honest with myself and I'm honest with you, I think in these five, six games, we have been for sure not lucky with Newcastle, with Everton, even with Nottingham and tonight as well.

"A lot of things, because the first goal we conceded we didn't defend in the right way, and the second goal we could be closer with [Cody] Gakpo , but have to understand if we are in the right way or not, I think watching the game, the last three games, four games, maybe until minute 60 with Newcastle, I think we are in the right way.

"I believe in my players, I have a big confidence, a big opinion of my players, and when we arrive to find the click, to win a game, I think we enjoy with these players, because the qualities of the players are incredible."

articles.title: England crush Sri Lanka to seal T20 series win
articles.summary: England comfortably chase a below-par target of 146 to thrash Sri Lanka by six wickets and seal the three-match T20 series with a game to spare.
articles.body:
Sri Lanka 145-9 (20 overs): Nissanka 37 (21); Dawson 3-32

England 146-4 (12.1 overs): Banton 52* (24); Rathnayake 1-25

England won by six wickets; lead series 2-0

England's impressive T20 form continued as they thrashed Sri Lanka by six wickets in Cardiff to seal the series with a match to spare.

Tom Banton's unbeaten 52 ensured England made light work of chasing a below-par 146, reaching the target in just 12.1 overs.

Jos Buttler and Aneurin Donald raced to an opening stand of 51 in 4.3 overs before they both fell in the space of four balls for 30 and 21 respectively, but England's middle order followed suit in their aggression.

Captain Harry Brook needed to score 49 to break Tilak Varma's record of 336 T20 international runs without being dismissed, and he looked on course, whacking three sixes in his 23 off just eight balls, before he was brilliantly caught by a diving Eshan Malinga.

Banton then took on the charge, clubbing four sixes in his 24-ball knock as England remain unbeaten in the shortest format this summer.

Brendon McCullum's side have now won 22 of their past 25 completed T20s since the start of last summer - a win percentage of 88%, with India (73%) the next best among full-member nations.

England's fluency juxtaposed Sri Lanka's innings as the tourist batters struggled again, limping to 145-9 after being bowled out for just 135 in the opener on Tuesday.

There will be added frustration from this innings, though, as their openers started so brightly by reaching 55-0 from the first five overs.

But Liam Dawson took two wickets in the final over of the powerplay to halt their momentum and the middle order failed to recover, losing 9-90 thereafter and adding just 12 from a dire final four overs.

Dawson finished with 3-32 and Jamie Overton 2-23, while Sonny Baker impressed again with his pace and control in a miserly spell of 1-15, including a wicket maiden in the 19th over.

The series concludes at Old Trafford on Saturday and is followed by three one-day internationals.

Dawson and Banton lead England dominance

Though it is proving to be a mismatched series so far, England are building a well-balanced line-up under Brook's leadership and have barely broken sweat in notching a 2-0 lead.

Sri Lanka's explosive start, led by Pathum Nissanka, who top-scored with 37, was the only time England have been on the back foot, but it was the ever-reliable Dawson who dragged it back, having become a mainstay in Brook's T20 line-up.

The two soft dismissals highlighted Sri Lanka's woes - Lahiru Udara was caught at mid-on and Kamil Mishara chipped one straight back to the slow left-arm spinner.

What followed was a series of soft dismissals, most caught trying to find the boundary, as Overton and Baker hammered away at a good length before Archer, who had started expensively, claimed two wickets at the death to revive his own figures.

Sri Lanka managed just two sixes in their innings compared to England's 10, with it being only the seventh time their top five have all hit at least one in T20 internationals.

Newcomer Donald started the carnage, ramping Dushmantha Chameera's first ball over the ropes, before Buttler joined the party and Brook then launched three of his own into the stands.

England's intent was clear from the fact Donald's strike-rate of 161.54 was the lowest of the top five. Spinner Wanindu Hasaranga took most of the damage as he conceded 42 off just three overs, with a couple disappearing out of the ground.

Banton, one of few batters to miss out in England's 254-4 on Tuesday, made the most of his opportunity to produce a fine finish by sweeping and striking firmly down the ground.

England have set themselves up nicely to finish unbeaten in T20s this summer after thrashing India 4-0 earlier in the year.
authors: Ffion Wynne - BBC Sport journalist in Cardiff

articles.title: Phillies news: This take on Jesus Luzardo's injury concern will catch fans' attention
articles.summary: With the Philadelphia Phillies looking to make noise in the playoffs, which are right around the corner, the team still hasn’t released information on the r...
articles.body:
With the Philadelphia Phillies looking to make noise in the playoffs, which are right around the corner, the team still hasn't released information on the return of injured star pitcher Jesus Luzardo . As Luzardo was placed on the injured list (IL) by the Phillies before the postseason, this MLB insider shares a concern that could scare fans.

Speaking on "Foul Territory," league insider Ken Rosenthal pointed out that, with no status yet for Luzardo in the playoffs, he found a statistic that could have some fans blaming Philadelphia for the current shoulder injury. He found that in Luzardo's last nine starts, he "threw more pitches during that time frame than anyone in the majors."

"In his last nine starts before he was injured, he threw more pitches during that time frame than anyone in the majors. Theoretically, it was not anything he could handle. Most in his career, over a nine-start span, but it led to this shoulder issue," Rosenthal said.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

More on the shoulder injury to Phillies' Jesus Luzardo

Rosenthal would then speak on how, before the Phillies acquired Luzardo from the Miami Marlins , the Chicago Cubs had been interested, and even "backed out of a deal" for him due to medicals they weren't comfortable with. However, those were back and elbow issues, as Rosenthal mentioned, with him relaying that Philadelphia doesn't believe that the injury is that serious.

"They don't believe it's terribly serious, and they don't believe he will be out for the postseason," Rosenthal said. "But certainly, their prospect of dominating the postseason, perhaps with their rotation, is less of a situation than it was earlier. Probably looking at [Aaron] Nola as the No. 3 and not Luzardo, and [Cristopher] Sanchez hasn't been as good down the stretch. So, it's a much greater concern for the Phillies than it was earlier."

So far this season for Philadelphia, Luzardo has recorded a 2.87 ERA and a 1.08 WHIP with 221 strikeouts and a 14-5 record in 29 starts.

At any rate, it remains to be seen when Luzardo can return to the Phillies and if it'll be just in time for the playoffs.

articles.title: The Sharks sign coach Ryan Warsofsky to a contract extension
articles.summary: The San Jose Sharks signed coach Ryan Warsofsky on Thursday to a multiyear contact extension on the first day of training camp before his third season at the...
articles.body:
SAN JOSE, Calif. (AP) — The San Jose Sharks signed coach Ryan Warsofsky on Thursday to a multiyear contact extension on the first day of training camp before his third season at the helm.

The 37-year-old Warsofsky had a 59-85-20 record in his first two seasons with San Jose as he has helped the rebuilding team get to the brink of the playoffs.

Warsofsky thanked owner Hasso Plattner, general manager Mike Grier and team president Jonathan Becher for giving him his first shot at being a head coach in the NHL and believes the team is ready to end a seven-season playoff drought.

"The goal when we took over was to make this team relevant again and start being more competitive," he said. "We've taken some steps. I give a lot of credit to Mike to bring in the right people. You don't change a culture with one person. You change it with a lot different people and a lot of the right people and we've done that."

The Sharks improved by 34 points last season for the 10th best single-season jump in the last 30 years. They finished four points out of the playoffs last season but come into this season with playoff expectations thanks to superstar Macklin Celebrini .

Grier said he wanted to get the extension done before the season so Warsofsky could focus on the team on the ice.

"It gives him a little bit of peace of mind to go out there and do his job without maybe having this hanging over his head a little bit if things don't go well to start the season," Grier said. "I think he's shown enough here in his time here in these four years even as an assistant that he can do the job, so I think the timing just worked out that we wanted to get ahead of it before the season."

Warsofsky is the NHL's youngest active head coach and has had success at nearly every level of hockey he has coached at in his career. He won a gold medal at the world championships with Team USA in 2025, as well as a Calder Cup title as both a head coach and assistant in the AHL.

Grier believes Warsofsky is still growing as a coach and praised his work with both superstars like Celebrini, as well as in developing other players in the middle or bottom of the lineup.

"He's a very good teacher," veteran forward Tyler Toffoli said. "He takes the time to make sure that we understand what's going on. He's already starting from day one this year. He is a great motivator. He's very passionate and he wants to win. You can see at times last year he was borderline devastated and at times he was on the moon. He's very passionate and he wants to win as much as we do on the ice."

articles.title: Travis Kelce Named as Victim in $35 Million Ponzi Scheme—Where Fraudster Splashed Out on Luxe Apartments and Hotel Stays
articles.summary: The Kansas City Chiefs tight end, 36, was named by prosecutors during the sentencing of Siddharth Jawahar.
articles.body:
Travis Kelce has been identified as a victim of a sprawling $35 million Ponzi scheme that saw the man behind the fraud use investor funds to help finance a lavish lifestyle that included luxury apartments, private jet travel, and high-end hotel stays.

The Kansas City Chiefs tight end , 36, was named by prosecutors during the sentencing of Siddharth Jawahar , the founder of Texas-based investment company Swiftarc Capital LLC, according to First Alert 4 .

Jawahar, 38, was sentenced to 11 years in federal prison on Sept. 15 after pleading guilty in January to three counts of wire fraud.

U.S. District Judge Zachary M. Bluestone also ordered Jawahar to pay $31.35 million in restitution to his victims.

While Kelce was identified in court as one of the people affected by the scheme, prosecutors did not reveal how much money the NFL star invested or how much he may have lost.

First Alert 4 reported that prosecutors declined to elaborate on Kelce's connection to the case, explaining that they do not comment on individual victims.

However, Kelce had previously been publicly linked to Swiftarc. A 2021 Forbes article identified the football player as an investor in a fund created by the company.

Jawahar's scheme stretched several years and involved tens of millions of dollars entrusted to his investment operation.

According to the Department of Justice, Jawahar began putting client funds into Philip Morris Pakistan in 2015, with approximately 99% of client money eventually concentrated in that single investment.

When its value declined, authorities said Jawahar concealed the losses from his clients and continued providing them with false information suggesting that their investments were profitable.

Other investors were led to believe their money had been placed into specific companies when those investments had not actually been made, prosecutors said.

Between July 2016 and December 2023, Jawahar collected more than $35 million from Swiftarc investors, according to federal authorities.

Of that amount, only about $10 million was actually invested.

Prosecutors said Jawahar diverted other investor funds toward making payments to existing clients and supporting his expensive personal lifestyle.

His spending extended to real estate and travel, with authorities citing luxury apartments in New York City and Austin, TX, as well as private jet trips and stays at upscale hotels.

Investor money also went toward memberships at private clubs around the country, shopping sprees, and expensive restaurant outings, according to prosecutors.

Jawahar was indicted in December 2023 before pleading guilty to three counts of wire fraud in January 2026.

Federal prosecutors also accused Jawahar of attempting to interfere with the investigation after he was indicted, including trying to persuade a victim to provide a favorable statement to the FBI and attempting to have his sister remotely wipe his iPhone to conceal evidence.

During sentencing, Bluestone pointed to both the scale of the financial losses and the yearslong nature of the fraud.

The judge also cited Jawahar's failure to begin repaying his victims as a factor in determining his sentence.

Kelce's exact financial losses remain unknown, with prosecutors offering no further details about how much money the Chiefs star had invested with Swiftarc.

articles.title: Why the Chargers' pass rush stalled in Week 1 and the Week 2 fix
articles.summary: Why did the Chargers struggle to generate pressure in Week 1, and how will they adjust to disrupt the Raiders quarterback Kirk Cousins?
articles.body:
The Chargers failed to generate much pressure in Week 1 against the Cardinals , which contributed to their defensive struggles in Chris O'Leary's play-calling debut. Los Angeles generated a 25% pressure rate (26th in the NFL) and only 20.7% without blitzing (30th).

The core issue was timing. Quarterback Jacoby Brissett averaged just 2.56 seconds to get the ball out (third-fastest in Week 1), while the Bolts' pass rush averaged 2.82 seconds to pressure the quarterback, according to Next Gen Stats.

Individually, Tuli Tuipulotu logged three pressures on 22 pass-rush snaps. By contrast, Khalil Mack saw more volume (31 pass-rush snaps) but only two pressures. Elsewhere, contributions were thin: Akheem Mesidor , Jamaree Caldwell , Daiyan Henley , Bud Dupree , Derwin James Jr., and Del'Shawn Phillips each finished with a single pressure.

The Chargers blitzed (5+ rushers) on only 10 of 39 dropbacks, according to Sumer Sports. They got pressure on five of those 10 snaps (50%) versus seven of the 29 non-blitz snaps and picked up their only sack of the matchup on a blitz in the fourth quarter. Arizona still completed half of those blitzed throws (5 of 10), averaged 7.0 yards per attempt, and the plays were worth a positive 0.185 EPA.

Heading into Week 2, the Chargers will face quarterback Kirk Cousins and the Raiders . Cousins was pressured on nine of 31 dropbacks in the Raiders' opener, and he took zero sacks but got the ball out in an average of 2.90 seconds, holding it noticeably longer than Brissett did. That extra half-second window is exactly what a pass rush that averaged 2.82 seconds to arrive last weekend needs.

Simulated pressures and disguised blitzes would help a lot. Cousins saw nine blitz snaps in Week 1 and was pressured on four of those snaps, a 44% pressure rate. Additionally, defensive line stunts and twists are imperative. Cousins is a pure pocket passer with virtually zero mobility. Internal pressure that collapses the pocket at his feet is the absolute fastest way to force him to crumble.

On the back end, coverage disguises are a must and cornerbacks need to press at the line of scrimmage more to disrupt the timing of quick-game concepts. If they force Cousins to hold the ball and look downfield, which is where he seems to struggle throwing (1-for-7 on passes longer than 10 yards against Miami ), the pass rush gets the extra split second it needs to get home.

articles.title: Steelers WR Roman Wilson Gets Major Vote of Confidence From Aaron Rodgers
articles.summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers opened their season with a 20-13 victory over the Atlanta Falcons in Week 1. For the Steelers, Roman Wilson stepped into a notable ro...
articles.body:
The Pittsburgh Steelers opened their season with a 20-13 victory over the Atlanta Falcons in Week 1. For the Steelers, Roman Wilson stepped into a notable role as the team's WR3 , giving quarterback Aaron Rodgers an active downfield option within the passing game.

However, Rodgers' complete reaction provides additional insight into Wilson's Week 1 showing and reveals how the veteran quarterback views the young wide receiver's development and potential moving forward.

Aaron Rodgers dismisses focus on Roman Wilson's target count

Wilson finished the Steelers' Week 1 win by catching three of his six targets for 26 yards. His six targets were tied for the second-most on Pittsburgh, while his involvement could have been even greater considering he also drew a defensive pass interference penalty on a deep pass during the first half.

When reporters questioned Rodgers about Wilson's number of targets, the Steelers quarterback made it clear that he was not concerned about where the receiver ranked on the team's target list.

"I don't give a sh*t about the target list," Rodgers said . "I don't care about any of that. I love Roman, (and) I think he's done a great job, you know. I think there's going to be a player too. That he makes that allows him to take off. But I thought he played fast last week, thought he played decisive, and I think he's just going to keep on getting better."

Despite receiving six targets, Wilson ran 29 routes compared to Michael Pittman Jr. 's 42, showing that he remains the Steelers' clear WR3 entering the season. That role could limit his opportunities, particularly in an offense that may not consistently produce high-scoring games.

Rodgers himself finished Week 1 with 221 passing yards, one touchdown and no interceptions. While discussing Wilson again, the Steelers quarterback reiterated his strong belief in the young receiver and expressed confidence that a breakout moment could eventually arrive.

"I love Roman. I think he's done a great job. You know, I think there's gonna be a play, too, that he makes…that allows him to take off, but I thought he played fast last week. I thought he played decisively, and I think he's just gonna keep on getting better."

Wilson endured an underwhelming start to his NFL career. He played only five snaps as a rookie after injuries disrupted his season before producing just 166 receiving yards and two touchdowns last season.

Still, Wilson has another opportunity to establish himself as a meaningful piece of Pittsburgh's offense, particularly with a new offensive system and Rodgers at quarterback. His Week 1 performance showed some encouraging signs, but with competition for opportunities and a limited number of routes, the young receiver will need to make the most of his chances as the season moves forward.

articles.title: US Olympic gold medal-winners asking for trades shakes up the NHL landscape
articles.summary: What happened in Milan did not stay in Milan.  It may have changed the course of NHL history.  Since the U.S. won gold at the Olympics in February, three mem...
articles.body:
What happened in Milan did not stay in Milan. It may have changed the course of NHL history.

Since the U.S. won gold at the Olympics in February, three members of that team asked for a trade and another was the subject of serious trade talk that did not materialize. Brady Tkachuk asked out of Ottawa and wound up in Florida to play with brother Matthew; Connor Hellebuyck could soon join him crossing the border after going public with his trade demand to leave Winnipeg ; and Dylan Larkin 's future in Detroit is in limbo following his desire for a fresh start.

Zach Werenski , who remains in Columbus , and fellow Americans on that team laugh at the idea that their group chat orchestrated all this. It is a bit of a coincidence it happened at the same time, but players get why people are making the connection between the trade requests and the Olympics.

"If you look at it from an outsider's perspective, like I understand it because it's like a lot of American guys, obviously, and the whole situation with the Olympics and winning and guys asking out and whatnot," Werenski said. "For a lot of us, that gold medal was the first taste of winning, and I think that's just what amplifies in your mind is like, 'I want to do this more.'"

Larkin has declined to share which teams he's willing to be traded to, would not say if his request to be moved still stands or if he wants to stay with the team. The Red Wings own the longest active playoff drought in the league, having not made it since Larkin's rookie year in 2015-16, a first-round exit.

In Hellebuyck's 10 years in Winnipeg, the Jets have not been past the second round since 2018 and he criticized team leadership after last season came to a close without a trip to the playoffs. He has said only that "moving on" is best for him and his family.

Tkachuk was the Senators' captain and brushed off the notion that his request had anything to do with wanting to play in the U.S. instead.

"I wouldn't say there's a big differential from Canada to (the) U.S.," Tkachuk said. "I think every individual's thought process, decision is a little bit different."

Teaming up with his brother makes the move more understandable to U.S. Olympic teammate and ex-Senators teammate Jake Sanderson .

"The way I look at it, I'm not surprised that Brady would want to go play with his brother," Sanderson said. "I don't think anybody should be surprised, so I don't blame him for that."

For Werenski, it is about chasing the Stanley Cup. He won the Norris Trophy as the league's top defenseman last season but in a decade with the Blue Jackets have made the playoffs just five times and advanced only once.

"You see your friends having success and guys winning Cups and you're so happy for them, but you want that to be you," Werenski said. "You put so much work in and so many hours and time and all this and you want to be in those games and have a chance at it, right? There's a lot of great players that will never win a Stanley Cup. But you want a crack at it. You want a chance to play for it."

There has been plenty of buzz about the Hughes brothers wanting to play together like the Tkachuks; they've said so . Quinn, who was dealt across the border from Vancouver to Minnesota in December before starring for the U.S. in Milan, does not have a contract beyond this season and could soon become the highest-paid player in the NHL, with the Wild or elsewhere.

"It is my life: I'm not going to do anything to make someone else happy," Hughes said. "Everyone's got to do what makes them happy, and then where the chips fall, they fall."

The hockey landscape could look much different a year from now, depending on what Hughes does and if U.S. Olympic captain Auston Matthews decides he'd like a change of scenery. On Wednesday, Matthews said his intent was always to stay in Toronto , and he has two years left on his contract.

Players are exercising power with requests

Larkin and Hellebuyck each have five seasons remaining on deals signed in 2023. Despite being signed long term, each took the risk of asking for a trade.

"Players now, I feel like, hold a whole lot of the cards," said Buffalo's Tage Thompson , who played with them at the Olympics. "And if they feel like it's the best decision for them, that's, I think, the route players are starting to go."

Werenski said he's happy where he is. Sanderson affirmed he's good in Ottawa, where he's signed through 2032.

What happens to others with gold medals displayed in their homes remains to be seen. But golden goal-scorer Jack Hughes doesn't attribute this trend to what he and his teammates accomplished.

"Even if the Olympics happened or didn't, I think those things would still unfold how they did with the guys that are requested to leave or whatever happened," Hughes said. "But definitely pretty funny with how everything shook out."

articles.title: Man City teenager Floyd Samba scores 2 goals in 5-0 win over Norwich in League Cup
articles.summary: Teenager Floyd Samba scored twice in his first-team debut to help Manchester City beat second-division Norwich 5-0 in the English League Cup on Thursday.  Al...
articles.body:
MANCHESTER, England (AP) — Teenager Floyd Samba scored twice in his first-team debut to help Manchester City beat second-division Norwich 5-0 in the English League Cup on Thursday.

Allan, a 22-year-old Brazilian forward, also marked his first City game with a goal, netting early in the second half as Enzo Maresca's team advanced to a fourth-round matchup against Brighton .

Rayan Cherki , the only City player who retained his place in the starting lineup from Sunday's Manchester derby against United, also scored.

The 17-year-old Samba opened the scoring in the 29th, heading in a cross from Allan. Cherki was released by Ayyoub Bouaddi three minutes later and beat goalkeeper Daniel Grimshaw one on one.

Allan made it to 3-0 with a low left-footed shot shortly after the break, followed by Samba's second goal, which he curled in.

Another teenager, the 18-year-old forward Ryan McAidoo , came on as a substitute and finished the rout in the final minute for the defending League Cup champions.

On Wednesday, Brighton recovered from a two-goal deficit to eliminate United 3-2 at Old Trafford.

articles.title: Chargers' Daiyan Henley says he's more motivated than ever in 2026
articles.summary: Chargers linebacker Daiyan Henley is ready to show the NFL who he is.
articles.body:
Chargers linebacker Daiyan Henley is as motivated as ever in 2026.

After a strong 2025 campaign, Henley is ready to show the NFL what he can do. In a recent interview with Omar Navarro of Chargers.com , Henley said he's more motivated than ever to prove that he and the Chargers are for real.

"The reason why I would say more [motivated] than ever is because it's another year and another opportunity to do better," Henley said. "Another chance, another showing of who I really am out there on that field, on tape to display to the world.

"With opportunities missed in the past, like I said, we don't dwell on that," Henley added. "We move forward and that's all I see right now, opportunities in the future. I see opportunities now. I'm amped, I'm motivated and I can't wait to go."

The Chargers got off to a rough start to the season, losing to the Cardinals in an embarrassing Week 1 outing. However, with Week 2 on the horizon, they'll look to bounce back against their rivals, the Raiders .

The defense was a major concern after the season opener, and plenty of eyes will be on it in the upcoming matchup. Henley was one of the few bright spots on that side of the ball in Week 1, recording eight tackles and half a sack.

The 26-year-old will look to carry that momentum into Week 2 and get his team on the win column. In 2025, Henley led the team in total tackles with 103, adding 3.5 sacks and five pass breakups.

articles.title: World Series of Darts Finals 2026: Champion Michael van Gerwen beaten
articles.summary: Defending champion Michael van Gerwen falls to a 6-5 defeat by Daryl Gurney in the opening round of the World Series of Darts Finals in Amsterdam.
articles.body:
Defending champion Michael van Gerwen fell to a 6-5 defeat by Daryl Gurney in the opening round of the World Series of Darts Finals in Amsterdam.

Northern Ireland's Gurney raced into a 3-0 lead before the Dutch top seed reeled off five consecutive legs to put himself on the brink of victory.

However, Gurney, who was drafted in as a late replacement when Lourence Ilagan withdrew from the 32-man field, responded by taking the ninth leg.

And when Van Gerwen missed six match darts, he was able to level the match at 5-5 and win the decider with the throw.

Gurney will now take on England's Ross Smith in the last 16 on Saturday after he advanced past Kevin Doets 6-3.

World number one Luke Littler will get under way on Friday against former UK Open champion Danny Noppert, having recently whitewashed the Dutchman 6-0 on his way to winning the Czech Darts Open.

World number two Luke Humphries also emerged victorious in another England versus Netherlands encounter, progressing 6-4 against Jermaine Wattimena.

Dutch number one Gian van Veen gained a measure of revenge for the home fans with a 6-2 triumph over Chris Dobey.

Dirk van Duijvenbode fought back from 4-1 down to defeat Sweden's Viktor Tingstrom 6-4, while Ryan Searle threw four 180s as he dispatched former world champion Rob Cross 6-2.

Searle goes on to play Josh Rock, who won the last three legs to edge out Stephen Bunting 6-5.

Karel Sedlacek marked his debut at the tournament with a 6-4 win over New Zealander Ben Robb and will take on Van Veen next.

articles.title: World Series of Darts Finals: Michael van Gerwen loses to Daryl Gurney as Luke Humphries, Gian van Veen progress in first round
articles.summary: Michael van Gerwen's World Series of Darts Finals title defence came to an end in the first round as he was beaten by Daryl Gurney in a deciding-leg thriller; Luke Humphries and Gian van Veen won their opening matches as Josh Rock defeated Stephen Bunting 6-5
articles.body:
Van Gerwen missed six match darts at 5-4 up before being taken to a deciding leg which Northern Ireland's Gurney controlled despite boos and whistles from the Amsterdam crowd.

It is just the second time Van Gerwen has lost his first match at the event as his difficult 2026 season continued.

"It was really hard work. I can't remember the last time I won on a major stage," said Gurney, who has largely struggled to perform on the big stage in recent years outside of the World Cup of Darts.

"I put my darts away tice because Michael had six [match] darts. In all honesty, I was very lucky to even go 5-5 and I had the throw I was like 'please I need trebles'."

Gurney earned a late call-up to the World Series of Darts Finals after visa issues caused Philippines players Alexis Toylo and Lourence Ilagan to withdraw.

Netherlands' Maik Kuivenhoven and Gurney were the highest-ranked players on the reserve list, so replaced the Philippines duo.

Gurney raced into a 3-0 lead as Van Gerwen did not even get a dart at double but the match swung quickly as the three-time world champion won the next five legs and looked on course for victory.

However, Gurney stopped the rot to make it 5-4 then capitalised on Van Gerwen's half a dozen missed match darts to break throw and held his nerve to book a spot in the second round against Ross Smith , who beat Kevin Doets 6-3 earlier.

Humphries battles through as Rock beats Bunting

Also on Thursday, Luke Humphries battled past Dutchman Jermaine Wattimena 6-4 in another dramatic contest.

The opening four legs were shared before Humphries broke with a spectacular 132 checkout (bullseye, bullseye, double 16).

However, at 5-3 up, Humphries missed eight match darts but managed to get over the line, after missing three more match darts in the next leg, to set up a meeting with Dirk van Duijvenbode in Saturday afternoon's second round. Van Duijvenbode had earlier fought back from 4-1 down to beat Sweden's Viktor Tingstrom 6-4.

Josh Rock also made a comeback to defeat Stephen Bunting 6-5 by winning the last three legs after the latter missed match darts.

Rock will play Ryan Searle , who cruised past Rob Cross 6-2, while Gian van Veen beat Chris Dobey 6-2 and Karel Sedlacek saw off Ben Robb 6-4 in the other matches.

On Friday, the first round will conclude with Luke Littler, Gerwyn Price, Jonny Clayton, James Wade and Nathan Aspinall among those in action.

Littler has won every major title this year and will look to continue his remarkable record by winning the World Series of Darts Finals for a second time.

articles.title: Husker Volleyball Hosts North Carolina on the Last Weekend of Non-Conference Matches
articles.summary: Husker volleyball is coming off of a sweep of in-state rival #20 Creighton on Wednesday night and now return to the Bob Devaney Center for the remainder of t...
articles.body:
Husker volleyball is coming off of a sweep of in-state rival #20 Creighton on Wednesday night and now return to the Bob Devaney Center for the remainder of their season. While PBA is fun to play in, Devaney is their home and is an electric environment.

This year has Devaney has been a little too quiet though. Quiet enough for Harper Murray and Dani Busboom Kelly to point it out in press conferences. Strap on your running shoes, warm up your voices and get rid of those oxygen machines, if possible, and be loud for this team. That is what they expect. That is the tradition that has been set. We can't be a hard environment to play in if it's going to be silent in moments where the team needs us.

The Huskers play another ranked opponent, #25 North Carolina, on Friday night. This will be their last ranked test of the non-conference schedule and also their last weekend before B1G play starts next Friday night when they host Rutgers.

North Carolina Tar Heels (4-2) 2025 Record: 22-9 2025 Conference Record: ACC (14-6) Last NCAA Tournament Appearance: 2025 (Lost to Wisconsin in 2nd Round)

The Tar Heels are coming off of a 2025 season where they were able to make it to the 2nd Round of the Tournament and a season that included a win against, at the time, #7 SMU during the regular season. UNC doesn't have an easy conference to play in either.

The ACC is regarded as, normally, the 2nd best conference behind the B1G. Some SEC enthusiasts like to say their conference is the best, but who do they really have this season? I can really only think of Kentucky since Texas and Texas A&M seem to kind of be flops this year. The ACC has firepower and usually does every year.

North Carolina may be ranked, but so are the other 4 teams above them in the preseason ACC rankings. Stanford, Pitt, Louisville, and SMU take the top 4 sports in the poll while UNC follows them and then Georgia Tech and Miami come after the Tar Heels. This conference is going to be fun to watch this season.

The Tar Heels schedule hasn't been that impressive so far yet. They have wins against Davidson, UNCW, James Madison, and Colorado State. Their 2 losses came against #Kentucky and Vanderbilt. The only two Power teams they have played, they have lost. The Huskers will hopefully make that 3 losses to Power programs.

Senior OH Safi Hampton is one of the three big arms for the Tar Heels this season. She was named First Team All-ACC last season and was also apart of the AVCA Preseason Player of the Year Watchlist. This season, Hampton already has a team high 65 kills, and is averaging 3.10 kills/set. She also adds 46 digs and 7 blocks.

5th Year OH/OPP Chelsea Thorpe is also an upperclassmen who has contributed a lot to the Tar Heel team since she got there in 2024. Thorpe started her career at Ohio State in 2022, but redshirted her freshman year. She is a big contributor on offense with 55 kills, 2.62 kills/set, but is also a big defensive help as well with 17 blocks.

The third head of the Tar Heel offense is Sophomore OH Bridget Malone. Malone is an underclassmen and seems to be the teams next top player, offensively, when Thorpe, and possibly Hampton, are gone next season. She is second in kills on the team with 56, 2.95 kills/set. She has only accumulated 20 errors on 149 swings taken.

This match will be North Carolina's second real test of the season after failing their first one by getting swept by Kentucky. They are hanging on by a thread in the rankings right sitting at #25 and a loss to Nebraska could mean they are unranked going into next week.

After being sick on Wednesday night for the match vs. Creighton, Manaia Ogbechie will hope to be back in the starting line up. If she still happens to be sick, the team will be just fine as Kenna Cogill looked like a seasoned pro against the Bluejays.

These teams will meet for only the 3rd time ever for Friday's match. It will begin at 7:00pm CST at the Bob Devaney Center and will be televised on B1G Network.

articles.title: The Dodgers have won the NL West again. Now what? 4 biggest questions entering playoffs
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Dodgers are NL West champions again, but several big questions remain unanswered ahead of the postseason.
articles.body:
It's the Dodgers ' fifth straight NL West title and 13th in the last 14 years.

The San Francisco Giants are the only team to interrupt the streak, winning the division title in 2021.

"There are a lot of unforeseen things, but I'm proud of all the contributors," Dodgers manager Dave Roberts told SportsNet LA after the game. "… It's another box that's checked, but there's still a lot of work to be done."

The Dodgers' 14 straight playoff appearances is tied for the most in MLB history with the Atlanta Braves (1991-2005). The magic number to clinch a first-round bye is six.

"(We) just keep going and eliminate distractions," Roberts said. "(We have to) keep the blinders on."

MLB teams ranked by their World Series championships

There are still plenty of hurdles Los Angeles will have to overcome before securing a third straight World Series title.

Only two other organizations have accomplished the feat: The New York Yankees and the Athletics . The Yankees have achieved at least a three-peat three times in their illustrious history.

The Yankees won four straight from 1936-39, five consecutive titles from 1949-1953 and most recently completed a three-peat from 1998-2000. The Athletics won three straight titles from 1972-1974.

Here's the four biggest questions facing the Dodgers as they prepare for the playoffs:

Ohtani's status remains uncertain as the postseason approaches, due to knee and biceps issues. He started his swing progression off a tee on Sept. 15. He could make his return to the lineup as a designated hitter as early as Sept. 23.

Andrew Friedman, the Dodgers' president of baseball operations, told reporters on Thursday that Ohtani is "progressing well."

The two-way star is expected to return in time for the playoffs but remains unlikely to pitch this season. Despite an effort to try and get him back on the mound, he's been unable to progress further.

The Dodgers had declared Ohtani not healthy enough to take the mound after he participated in a short bullpen session on Aug. 28 and threw close to 20 pitches.

Will Dodgers' roster age and injuries be a concern?

The average age for the Dodgers' roster is 30.6 years old, which is the highest in MLB, just ahead of the Chicago Cubs (30.4) and Atlanta Braves (30.3).

Pitcher Blake Treinen is the oldest player on the roster at 38 years old. Miguel Rojas is the next oldest at 37 years old. Rojas has already stated this will be his last season as an active player.

The Dodgers have managed to add some younger talent to the roster to help finish out the season and gain experience.

They've leaned on Josue De Paula, who was considered the team's top prospect, to serve as the designated hitter in Ohtani's latest absence.

The 21-year-old made his major-league debut on Sept. 11 at LoanDepot Park, becoming the youngest Dodgers player since Alex Verdugo on Sept. 2, 2017.

De Paula's bat could become a necessity depending on the status of several other veterans, including Mookie Betts , Freddie Freeman and Kiké Hernández .

Freeman has produced big moments for the Dodgers in the World Series, but the 37-year-old's status in the days leading up to the postseason is worth monitoring. He's considered day-to-day with right knee soreness caused by patellar tendinitis.

Pitcher Edwin Diaz and outfielder Andy Pages could be inching closer to a return and could be activated during the team's upcoming homestand.

Who will make up Dodgers' pitching rotation?

The Dodgers made a big splash, acquiring Tarik Skubal ahead of the trade deadline.

Skubal, Yoshinobu Yamamoto , Blake Snell and Tyler Glasnow project as the starters for the first four games of a seven-game series.

Yamamoto has remained fairly healthy throughout the season, posting a 14-8 record with a 2.51 ERA in 27 starts.

Skubal was placed on the injured list in May 2026 due to loose bodies in his left elbow that required surgery. The two-time Cy Young Award winner has produced a 10-7 record with a 2.70 ERA in 24 starts.

Snell also had loose bodies removed from his elbow that caused him to miss three months before returning in early August. He also missed some time earlier this season with shoulder fatigue. His latest start was cut short after one inning on Sept. 16 due to groin tightness.

The two-time Cy Young Award winner has a 4-1 record and a 1.86 ERA in eight starts.

Glasnow went on the 60-day injured list this season due to a lower back spasm. He returned to the rotation in late August. He did not have an opportunity to participate in the 2024 World Series run due to right elbow tendinitis, but he played a vital role in winning the title in 2025.

The Atlanta Braves or San Diego Padres appear to be the Dodgers' most likely first opponent in the MLB playoffs. The Braves have gotten the best of the Dodgers this season, winning five of six games.

The Dodgers have produced better results against the Padres, winning seven of 10 games this season. The Dodgers will host the Padres for a three-game series Sept. 22-24.

articles.title: Jim Harbaugh Sends Clear Message on Raiders & Maxx Crosby
articles.summary: Los Angeles Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh had a lot to say about the upcoming matchup with the Las Vegas Raiders. The post Jim Harbaugh Sends Clear Messag...
articles.body:
Coming off a Week 1 win, the Las Vegas Raiders face a tougher test in Week 2. They're headed on the road to face the Los Angeles Chargers , a team they've lost four straight games to.

The Chargers are going to be highly motivated after getting embarrassed by the Arizona Cardinals in Week 1. Jim Harbaugh's first NFL coaching job came with the Raiders, so he may have a little extra juice heading into the game.

This is also both teams' first division rivalry game of the season. The Raiders are technically on the road, but when they come to Los Angeles , it's a home game for them.

That hasn't helped them win at SoFi Stadium, as they've lost the last seven games they've played there. Beating the Chargers would be a big statement for the Raiders and prove that Week 1 wasn't just a fluke against a bad team.

Harbaugh was impressed with how the Raiders looked against the Dolphins and isn't underestimating what they can do.

"They had an outstanding start," Harbaugh told reporters. "A lot of really good players playing really well. Really well coached. Coach Kubiak, he's got them going. It's a big challenge, a big test, a division game, Raider Week. It's got it all."

Defensive end Maxx Crosby loves playing the Chargers. He's had a lot of success playing against the team. He had a strong start to the season after an offseason filled with trade rumors and injury rehab.

He's the type of defensive player who can wreck an offensive game plan. He's a player that Harbaugh has gained a lot of respect for.

"He's earned the respect that everybody in football has for him," Harbaugh said. "Play style, the way he plays, the disruptive nature."

Offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel has faced Crosby before, but he's hoping that he doesn't bring his best play to Los Angeles.

"He is relentless and I enjoy the challenge, but it would be cool if he was tired and wanted to take a nap," McDaniel told reporters .

The Raiders haven't had any success against the Chargers since Harbaugh came to Los Angeles. The Chargers have made the playoffs in back-to-back years and are still considered one of the better teams in the AFC despite the Week 1 loss.

Week 1 can get weird, so it's possible the Chargers are much better than what they looked like on tape. That doesn't mean the Raiders can't beat them.

Las Vegas' offense and defense both look really strong in Week 1. If Ashton Jeanty can have another 100-yard game and Crosby can get after Justin Herbert consistently, the Raiders will have a good chance to win.

Having tight end Brock Bowers back would also help quite a bit. He missed Week 1, but there's some hope he could be ready for the Chargers. That would certainly help the Raiders score more points. It'll be a tough matchup, but the Raiders can prove a lot of doubters wrong with a win over their hated rival.
