articles.title: Athlete of the Week: 3 pairs of brothers on Phillis Wheatley HS football team play for each other
articles.summary: For ABC13's Athlete of the Week segment, we showcase three pairs of brothers on the same football team for Phillis Wheatley High School.
articles.body:
The Dorsey brothers are ready to go when it comes to football for Phillis Wheatley High School.

"It's good, fun, a lot of energy when we are all together," Phillis Wheatley HS senior Larry Dorsey said.

What makes the family unique is that there are three pairs of brothers on the team, all cousins, six players in all.

"If I don't make a play, I know one of my other family members will come, you know, and clean up the play for me," Vincent Dorsey said.

"I call them by their first names," Wheatley HS head coach Deandre Cooper said. "If I called out Dorsey, I might look up, and all five or six of them are right in front of me."

On offense, you can find brothers Peter and Maurice blocking for cousins Vincent and Larry.

"It's like having another brother," junior Peter Dorsey said. "Backyard football, it just feels the same."

"We've known each other for a long time; since we were young, we've been around each other," freshman Maurice Dorsey said.

On defense, it's not uncommon to have all six Dorseys on the field at the same time.

"I know I can trust them," senior Cameron Dorsey said. "I can go to them when I need any help or when I need to study film, or I need to remember the plays. I know I can always go to them, as they are the best for me."

"I've been playing with them for a long time," Sophomore Kendrick Dorse added.

"It's my first time really being on the team with a lot of family members, so it feels different; it feels good just to know every one of my cousins is making a play every game," Kendrick's brother Vincent said.

To the Dorseys, team success matters most. They try not to let family disagreements get in the way of helping the team win or the bond they share.

"We'll have an argument here and there because we are family; we've known each other for a long time," Peter Dorsey said. "It'll all come down to the end; we love each other."

articles.title: With Lucas Museum About to Open, Mellody Hobson Steps Down From LA28 Olympics Board
articles.summary: Just days before the Lucas Museum of Narrative Art opens to the public, co-founder Mellody Hobson has stepped down from the board of directors of Los Angeles...
articles.body:
Just days before the Lucas Museum of Narrative Art opens to the public, co-founder Mellody Hobson has stepped down from the board of directors of Los Angeles Olympics organizing committee LA28, Variety has confirmed.

Hobson indicated that the demands of overseeing the Lucas Museum, which opens Tuesday after a Friday gala, were too great to continue serving on the board, according to an email reviewed by LAist . Business executive Hobson is co-founder of the museum with her husband George Lucas.

The 35-person board is led by Casey Wasserman, who was forced to give up his stake of his management company after the Epstein files revealed his messages with Ghislaine Maxwell.

An activist group called the Fair Games Coalition has sought to meet with Hobson over their concerns about the Olympics and Paralympics, including housing and workers' needs. The coalition is also concerned about the games' effect on the South Los Angeles area that is home to the Lucas Museum.

"The Fair Games Coalition is deeply disappointed that Mellody Hobson responded to requests to meet with faith leaders, workers and community members calling for living wages, affordable housing, immigrant protections, and Games that benefit all Angelenos by announcing she was resigning from the LA28 Board," the group said in a statement.

"Mellody Hobson could have used her influence on the LA28 Board to stand with our communities, support living wages, and defend immigrant workers. Instead, she chose the easy way out. That is deeply disappointing," Rev. Gary Williams, Senior Pastor of St. Mark United Methodist Church, a member of the Fair Games Coalition, said in the group's statement.

articles.title: Everything Texans DC Matt Burke said ahead of Week 2's matchup vs. Bengals
articles.summary: Here's everything Houston Texans defensive coordinator Matt Burke said Thursday ahead of Week 2's matchup against the Cincinnati Bengals, including his thoug...
articles.body:
Here's everything Houston Texans defensive coordinator Matt Burke said Thursday ahead of Week 2's matchup against the Cincinnati Bengals , including his thoughts on the Bengals' wide receiver room, Joe Burrow 's athleticism, life without Henry To'oTo'o and more.

Question: On cleaning up mistakes in coverage

Matt Burke: "It was a technique thing more than anything. I wouldn't say we had just a lot of straight busts in terms of like guys not in sort of spots where they need to be. It was leverage stuff. It was some technique issues. It's been a huge focus this week and getting back to trying to play the type of football that we're used to playing. It's a new week. We're moving forward. We had to really spend some time making sure we're addressing what we saw to make sure that we don't put that performance out there again."

Q: On how the defense has responded to the Week 1 performance

Burke: "I feel like the guys responded well. There's obviously a lot of pride in that room and with that group. To a man, everyone almost was trying to shoulder the blame saying, 'I was the reason this happened. I didn't do this.' I was like, 'Hey, man, we're all in this together.' I think the mindset approach of that, guys really are taking it upon themselves to where can I improve and make sure that I'm not the one that's letting the defense down or letting the team down. I feel like there's been a really good focus on preparation this week. They've been really locked in. I think they're itching to get back out there and show what they're really made of."

Q: On whether the Buffalo Bills surprised the defense with new plays

Burke: "I wouldn't say that. I don't think there was a ton of un-scouted stuff that hit us. When we were getting some of the things that we were expecting to see, most of the plays we had seen or scouted, but it was sort of in the timings and the volumes of things that we were getting. I thought the guys did a good job at halftime of settling down a little bit. We came back out in the second half and put ourselves in a position to have the last drive to win the game, which we expect to close that game out when we got a lead with a couple minutes left. I thought they did do a good job of once we settled down, that we kind of turned it around a little bit in the second half and I'd like to close that game out there and correct the same mistakes from a win. But I think we'll hopefully put a better show out there this week."

Q: On CB Kamari Lassiter in practice this week

Burke: "Yeah, he's great. He's back to being Kamari. Like I said, I feel like that was to a man, there were probably seven, eight guys coming up to me. I felt like it was me. I didn't prepare you guys well or I didn't do this. Everyone was like, 'I'm sorry, man. I'm sorry.' There were like a lot of guys trying to take ownership of what happened. And again, it's not that. It's never that. It's a collective. For Kamari he's been bouncing around. There's not a lot to message. He's a great player. I expect him to make great plays and to do great things this year. He's going to perform the way he needs to perform."

Q: On S Reed Blankenship playing in a new system

Burke: "It's everybody. It's communication and him playing techniques that, again, it's not just singling him out. Everyone has to play the techniques that we're asking them to play and play with the leverage or play be in the spots where you're supposed to be. You can probably ask me about every single player on the defense, it's probably the same answer. We've all got to tighten up our focus, our techniques and what we're doing and what we're asking them to do and go see what that looks like."

Q: On how the Buffalo Bills slowed down the pass rush

Burke: "They committed a lot of resources to it, which they should. I don't think there was a ton of true drop back pass in that game. There were a lot of chips, they didn't leave edges open. They were committing six, seven, eight guys to the protectionary play. That was their plan of attack. We need to have answers to help get our guys loose in some of those situations. I think we tweaked a couple things in the second half that kind of started getting some loose. We had a little bit more pressure, a little bit more of interior stuff working when we got going into the game. They committed a lot of resources to make sure that those guys didn't wreck the game like they did last year."

Q: On what he has seen from the Cincinnati Bengals offense

Burke: "They're good players. Quarterback's really good. Operating at a high level. He can throw it open. He can make every throw in the book. He's really impressive, obviously, with a lot of weapons. Everyone knows about the receivers and what they're about. [TE Mike] Gesicki has a different element. A really tall, long receiving guy on the inside part of the field. I feel like maybe people have talked about it, but I have a lot of respect for the backs, man. Number 30 [RB Chase Brown ], I didn't have a lot of history with him in terms of knowing what he's about. But watching the tape, he really jumps out. He runs hard. He's north-south. Everyone's so concerned about dropping and getting underneath all the deep passing game that when he gets going in space, we have to be sure that we're not letting him get loose either. A lot of really good players on that team."

On whether he expects teams to copy the Buffalo Bills offensive attack

Burke: "I'm sure there are elements of everything. We saw stuff from Buffalo that Denver tried to do to us last year. There's always going to be a copycat league and there's always going to be things that are taken. Every team's personnel is different, so not everyone can operate the same way that a Buffalo does or that a Cincinnati does. They're going to have their own twists on how they want to do things. We know every week going into whatever game we're playing that people are going to be worried about our rush and they're going to have whatever their version of a plan is to try to manipulate the rush and slow it down. Whether it's getting the ball out quick or whether it's chipping or whether it's max protect, whatever their version of that is, like, we know we have to have a plan for that. From a philosophical standpoint, I would say that's something that we prepare for every week, but it looks different because not everyone has the same people or bodies or personnel to do some of the things that other teams do."

Burke: "He's been here for that long, you talk about trying to have someone that, not to stereotype Jake, but I think everyone's going to say he's, 'This or that athletically or whatever.' But he's a guy that's always in the right spot that knows the system. We just talked about being where you're supposed to be and doing the right things and being the right leverage. He's a guy that has grown in that role and embraced that. The guys played multiple positions for us in his time here. I would say he's been a pretty reliable player for us."

Q: On whether he feels Week 1 was humbling

Burke: "Of course. Anytime you get beat and give up a lot of points. I would say that's been one of our worst performances in the last few years. I would hope there's a humbling factor to that. But every week's different. We're trying to really control what we can control, which is focusing on getting better this week and game planning what we want to do. We have another really good offense. If we're going to be sitting here crying over spilled milk, that game's done, we can't do anything about it. If we're distracted by that, then we're probably not going to look as good this week either because we have a really good offense coming to town. The task for us as coaches and the players was to correct what we need to correct from that game. Is there stuff that may be show up again that we have answers for as it happens throughout the season? We have to a really good offense that have to prepare to shut down this week and it's going to take all our focus to do that. I think that's kind of been what we've tried to lean on."

Q: On Cincinnati Bengals QB Joe Burrow's skillset

Burke: "There are some quarterbacks to where if you think your coverage takes something away that they won't throw it, he'll still throw it. He trusts his arm. He trusts the receivers for sure. You may think, 'I'm clouding here. I'm rolling covers a certain way. Just by my presence, I'm taking this away, but that's not true here. You can't think that the coverage is necessarily even dictating where throws are going to go. Sometimes you can do that where we're putting seven guys over here and you're not throwing that side, you have to throw over here. Well, he doesn't care. He'll still think he can fit throws in. He probably makes more hole shots than any quarterback in the league, he can because he has the arm to do it and he trusts those guys to be in the right spot. I think you can't relax in that stuff where you sometimes think you might you have a down off, but like, I'm getting the coverage leaning to me or I'm getting favored by this call here. Well, that doesn't matter for him because he can make the throws and he believes he can make it and he trusts those guys to go make plays for him. We really have to be on our techniques and in our leverage and where we need to be because he'll certainly make you pay, if not. Even if you are sometimes. Not to go back to last week, but we had an opportunity to make some plays. We'll have some opportunities probably to make some plays. There's going to be some balls thrown up that it's going to be them versus us and we have to go make those plays."

Q: On not tackling in Training Camp and how that affects the regular season

Burke: "We try to train tackling without taking guys to the ground. How do you do that? You don't want to be sitting there banging, taking your players to the ground every play in practice in an OTA. A lot of it's about tracking and just trying to get to the angles of those things. I would probably say that's probably a fairly universal thing throughout the years in the league in terms of early in the season, you just haven't been able to have the opportunity to do those things. We try to stress getting to the right points, being in the right spot, tracking and being on the hip and then just the finishing part. I don't think that's our problem in terms of being physical when we get to the point of attack. As long as we're getting there and getting the right angles and taking the right leverage to get to those spots I feel like we'll be all right."

Burke: "Probably one of the encouraging things from last week. I thought 'JD' played really well. Obviously had the sack, had some production, had a couple pressures. He's a savvy football player. He's done it for a long time. He has a really just good feel for the game. When it shows up on game days, he's just got a knack for kind of being in the right spot and making some plays. Sometimes it's unorthodox, but he's always making those plays. It doesn't always look the same as maybe Will [Anderson Jr.] or [DE] Danielle [Hunter] or something, but he just kind of finds a way to be in the right spot and affect the play. He's such a unique athlete. He affected the game in a positive way, I would say."

Q: On how schemes that work against the defense can benefit down the line

Burke: "You always have to have those conversations. Honestly, I would say third down wasn't our problem. It's probably the one area statistically that we were decent. We just couldn't get them to third down. Some of that stuff was showing up on earlier downs. Some of the volume, where some of the plays were showing up were not in some of the situations maybe that we were anticipating. You always have to have contingencies for what's going on. As you move through the season, that bank of information grows. As you build out, 'This is how we're attacking this week. This is how this team saw us this week.' As you sort of build that bank of as we go through the season, if this comes up in Week 8, we have some answers for it and how do we plan to mitigate those situations."

articles.title: Steelers news: Patrick Queen doesn't know why Joey Porter Jr. is out, but he's on his side
articles.summary: Pittsburgh Steelers cornerback Joey Porter Jr.’s status remains uncertain after he left practice early on Thursday with a team trainer. Porter was seen taki...
articles.body:
Porter was seen taking part in the team stretch during the portion of practice open to the media. He also participated in at least one ball-security drill before leaving after only a few individual-work reps. His practice designation also shifted, with Thursday's report listing a back injury after Wednesday had him marked as limited for non-injury-related conditioning .

The back issue has followed Porter since the opening day of training camp, keeping him on the PUP list throughout camp in Latrobe. He was medically cleared before practice on Wednesday, when he returned in a limited capacity. Head coach Mike McCarthy had said Porter was expected to increase his workload Thursday after doing more Wednesday than he had the previous week.

Porter did not play in Pittsburgh's Week 1 win over the Atlanta Falcons after McCarthy determined that the cornerback needed additional time to ramp up. McCarthy has also remained noncommittal about whether Porter will be available Sunday against the New England Patriots .

The uncertainty surrounding Porter has also coincided with contract negotiations. The Steelers and Porter did not reach an extension before the regular-season deadline, leaving the 2023 second-round selection set to play the final year of his rookie deal.

Pittsburgh players have continued to support Porter Jr., with linebacker Patrick Queen the latest to do so, saying he respects him regardless of whether his absence is injury- or contract-related.

"Joey, whatever he's going through, whether it's injury or contract, I respect it," Queen said on Thursday. "I'm behind him 100%. I tell him every single time, 'I respect how you go about your business every single day. I know you all see the stuff he does out there. I definitely respect him."

The Steelers can use the franchise tag to keep him from reaching free agency in 2027. Pittsburgh is also the NFL's only team with a policy against negotiating contracts during the season.

The Steelers defense limited the Falcons to 143 passing yards, with Asante Samuel Jr . and Jamel Dean handling the cornerback duties against backup quarterback Cooper Rush.

articles.title: This Olympic river has 500 crocodiles in it - but that's not the main concern
articles.summary: Queensland's Fitzroy River has been selected for the 2032 Games, despite concerns over the course - and its inhabitants.
articles.body:
The annual rowing regatta for schools in the Australian state of Queensland usually passes off without too much attention.

This weekend more than 600 of the state's most promising teenage rowers are battling it out on the crocodile-inhabited Fitzroy River, in the city of Rockhampton.

"We've never had any media wanting to attend before," Anthea O'Loughlin, head of Rowing Queensland, tells the BBC.

But this year is different. In six years' time, the 2032 Brisbane Olympics and Paralympics are set to stage rowing and canoe sprint events in this very stretch of water, which has just passed a technical assessment and been endorsed as safe and fair for athletes.

While sightings of saltwater crocodiles on the river – which number around 500 and can grow to four metres (13ft) long – are not uncommon, state government files going back more than 40 years record no attacks by the reptiles on humans.

And though influential figures at last month's World Rowing congress in Amsterdam made occasional references to "safety", the presence of the reptiles was not their chief concern.

"Fairness" is what's been raised with British Rowing's chief executive Tom Solesbury – a reference to the tidal river's natural bends and currents, which many in the rowing community say make it unsuitable for elite competition.

Drew Ginn, who has won three Olympic gold medals for Australia in rowing, told the BBC he had concerns over potential flooding and "fairness and integrity" at the venue.

"Personally, I'm not fearful of the Australian animals but I've never had a crocodile near me," he said.

"I'm sure I'd row faster, I'm sure all the athletes would row faster. That's on the list of concerns, I don't think it's the highest priority in concerns but it was certainly cited very early on."

The German rowing body's president Moritz Petri said athletes had also questioned the sustainability of holding the event some 600km (373 miles) from Brisbane.

But the "so-called impediments" got short shrift from the most senior politician in Queensland, state premier David Crisafulli, who reached for less diplomatic language.

"Let's be honest, let's scratch beneath the surface and call it for what it is," he said days after the Amsterdam meeting.

"It is a group of interstate and overseas elites who are trying to bully their way because they don't want to go to regional Queensland and that's not right."

Rowing chiefs contacted by the BBC before Thursday's decision declined to comment directly on Crisafulli's "elites" remarks.

But both Petri and Simon Wickham, chief executive of Rowing New Zealand, said their concerns had nothing to do with regional or urban preference but with competitors getting fair racing.

Petri added it was about what's best for their athletes who will train four years for the event, "dreaming night [after] night of becoming an Olympic champion".

And Ginn said: "If elite means having some expertise in the sport over 20 odd years, I'm proud of that."

Whether it was crocs or currents that tipped the balance, ultimately it was the sport's governing body World Rowing and the International Olympic Committee (IOC) that had the final say on the river's suitability.

On Thursday they approved it after a technical assessment by an engineering firm and the Games' infrastructure authority – which looked at the riverbed, competition course, river flows, water levels and likely weather conditions during the Games.

"Based on the extensive analysis undertaken, we now know that the Fitzroy River is capable of providing fair competition conditions during the period of the Games," World Rowing president Jean-Christophe Rolland said.

There was also now "confidence" in the river for canoe sprint athletes, said Thomas Konietzko, president of that sport's governing body, Paddle Worldwide.

The state premier was delighted. "The Fitzroy has passed with flying colours," an upbeat Crisafulli told parliament. "It's official. Signed, sealed and delivered."

In backing Rockhampton, the state government ignored a 2025 report it commissioned itself, which found the location unsuitable and concluded the best option would be to use a course built in Sydney for the 2000 Olympics.

The Fitzroy now needs to pass a final assessment of its design, value for money and long-term community legacy. As the decision rests with the state government, it's unlikely to fall at this hurdle.

But a wider debate will continue over whether Rockhampton is the right place to invest heavily in rowing facilities – and whether it can accommodate the 2032 influx of visitors.

The city is surrounded by cattle producers and normally experiences its peak number of guests every three years during Beef Week.

They're not mentioned anywhere in the latest update from the IOC and World Rowing and they weren't referenced in the media release about the technical assessment. That report itself has not yet been made public.

The safety management plan for this weekend's school regatta does however mention the word "crocodile" 28 times.

"The Fitzroy River is within recognised crocodile country," it says.

"Event planning must therefore assume that a crocodile sighting is possible… No natural waterway in crocodile country can be guaranteed to be crocodile-free."

Procedures this weekend include suspending racing and competitors returning to the bank if a croc is spotted. The official signal for a sighting is the call of "crocodile, crocodile, crocodile".

Asked specifically about crocodiles, New Zealand's Wickham told the BBC the primary concern was ensuring the "fairest possible course" for rowers. "We would obviously expect any course chosen to be safe for rowers," he added.

The company owned by Australia's richest person Gina Rinehart, Hancock Prospecting, which supported Rockhampton's bid and has pumped tens of millions of dollars into sports including rowing, pointed to "fake media" concerns about risks posed by flooding and crocodiles in the Fitzroy.

"The people of Rocky for many years have sent their own children to train in this river, and for competitions, without a single crocodile incident," a spokesperson said in a statement.

And those who argue the tabloid-friendly crocodile debate is overblown, say the biggest of the creatures live downstream. The less-dangerous freshwater crocodiles are more likely to be spotted in the rowing arena, they say.

Also contested by government is the flood risk, though Rowing Queensland's O'Loughlin says that their schools event was due to be held on the Fitzroy in August 2024, but had to be moved after the course was washed away.

Brisbane 2032's chief executive has said organisers are making contingency plans "as we would for any venue".

The 2000 Olympics venue in Sydney is ready and waiting as a backup – though that would be unconscionable for Queenslanders.

For the school-age rowers at this weekend's regatta, none of this debate really matters as they take to the water.

Among them are potentially some contenders for the 2032 Games.

"For our students, the Fitzroy is first and foremost their home water," says Phillip Moulds, headmaster of The Rockhampton Grammar School.

"The Fitzroy has also been the starting point for many… some of whom have gone on to compete at the highest levels of the sport nationally and internationally."

articles.title: NBC to stream Big Ten game for free on YouTube this Saturday
articles.summary: Even before NBC and YouTube begin their partnership to bundle Peacock into YouTube Premium in early 2027, the two companies are finding ways to link up. This...
articles.body:
Even before NBC and YouTube begin their partnership to bundle Peacock into YouTube Premium in early 2027, the two companies are finding ways to link up. This weekend, that means NBC Sports will stream a Big Ten football game live on its YouTube channel at no cost.

On Saturday, NBC Sports will stream the Eastern Michigan-Wisconsin game live, for free, on its YouTube channel.

The stream is part of NBC's larger partnership with YouTube announced earlier this summer. As part of the deal integrating Peacock into YouTube Premium, NBC revealed that "a selection of live sporting events" would stream on their YouTube channel. At the time of the announcement, the network did not specify which events would be selected to stream on the Google-owned platform. Eastern Michigan-Wisconsin will mark the first event to stream on YouTube under the agreement.

The news is a great development for fans. Before the game showed up as scheduled on NBC Sports' YouTube channel, the only ways to watch would have been through Peacock or NBC Sports Network, the revived cable network that airs Peacock-exclusive live sports on a limited number of pay-TV providers. Now, Eastern Michigan and Wisconsin fans can catch the game for free on YouTube without paying for a Peacock subscription.

It's unclear if NBC plans to stream any more Big Ten football games on YouTube this season. Regardless, the decision to put Saturday's game on the platform shows there's at least a willingness to place somewhat notable inventory on YouTube, rather than only niche properties.

articles.title: Washington football eyeing four-star 2028 Georgia edge rusher
articles.summary: The Washington Huskies are making a concerted effort to recruit some of the top pass rushers in Georgia.
articles.body:
As the Washington Huskies continue building their board for the 2028 class, Jedd Fisch has made it clear he wants his program to recruit at a national level. After adding commitments from players in Texas, Oklahoma, Louisiana, New Jersey, and Florida between the 2026 and 2027 cycles, Washington is looking to Georgia as its next target.

During a 24-10 win over Washington State in the Apple Cup, the Huskies hosted four-star defensive lineman Isaac Kalubi-Lukuni and three-star Tory Clark for unofficial visits, and as defensive line coach Jason Kaufusi and edge rushers coach Aaron Van Horn take a long look at the state, four-star edge rusher Myles Tate also looks like a priority target for Washington.

The 6-foot-3, 225-pound product of Woodward Academy in Atlanta is ranked as the No. 103 overall prospect and No. 16 edge rusher in the 2028 class by 247Sports, and as the Huskies continue to prioritize a talent infusion on the edge, the two-sport athlete, who also stars on the baseball diamond, will be a difficult addition.

The coveted prospect holds 40 offers, with Alabama, Georgia, LSU, Miami, Notre Dame, and Oregon all among the programs in pursuit of his services, but as the Huskies continue to emphasize playing time for freshmen, Tate displays a skill set that could get him on the field early if he were to wind up on Montlake.

On film, Tate displays the ability to line up as either a standup outside linebacker or with his hand in the dirt, with several different ways to get to the quarterback. He possesses an explosive first step, along with a spin move, the power to work through blocks, and a motor that never gives up on a play.

After securing unofficial visits from several other Georgia prospects, Washington is likely looking to get Tate to Seattle at some point during the fall to have him experience a gameday atmosphere at Husky Stadium.

articles.title: Patriots rooting guide for NFL Week 2
articles.summary: Rooting information, kickoff times, TV schedule and more for NFL Week 2.
articles.body:
And just like that, the second week of the 2026 NFL regular season has arrived. The New England Patriots will enter the action on Sunday with a game against the Pittsburgh Steelers , one of 16 total games on the menu between Thursday and Monday.

Here's who to root for in the 15 contests not featuring Drake Maye and company.

Detroit Lions (1-0) at Buffalo Bills (1-0): Go Lions! The Patriots' biggest division rival started the season with a win. Naturally, a follow-up loss especially to an NFC side would be the preferred outcome. It happening at the first game at Buffalo's new state-of-the-art stadium would be the cherry on top. | Prime Video

Carolina Panthers (0-1) at Atlanta Falcons (0-1): Go good game! Neither team is on the Patriots' schedule or in any other way directly tied to the team. | FOX

New Orleans Saints (0-1) at Baltimore Ravens (1-0): Go Saints! While a Saints win would negatively impact the sixth-round draft pick the Patriots will get from them next year — shoutout Ja'Lynn Polk — it is the preferred outcome with the 2026 season in mind. | CBS

Minnesota Vikings (1-0) at Chicago Bears (1-0): Go Bears! With both on New England 's schedule, the tiebreaker goes to the team that has a more valuable Patriots draft pick tied to its fortunes. A Vikings loss would be good news for the seventh-round selection obtained as part of the Walter Rouse trade. But why not root for the Vikings then? Because the highest of the Patriots' two fifth-round picks — including the Bears pick received for Garrett Bradbury — will go to Philadelphia anyway via the conditions of the A.J. Brown move. | FOX

Cincinnati Bengals (1-0) at Houston Texans (0-1): Go Texans! The pick acquired through the Marte Mapu trade would suggest rooting for Cincinnati, but the desire for a close AFC playoff race forces us to go with Houston in this one. | CBS

Green Bay Packers (0-1) at New York Jets (1-0): Go Packers! NFC team over Patriots division rival. Easy choice. | FOX

Cleveland Browns (0-1) at Tampa Bay Buccaneers (0-1): Go Buccaneers! Another case of picking the NFC team over AFC team. | CBS

Philadelphia Eagles (1-0) at Tennessee Titans (0-1): Go Eagles! We are going NFC over AFC yet again, because there are no ties to the Patriots in this game as well. | FOX

Jacksonville Jaguars (1-0) at Denver Broncos (0-1): Go Broncos! The game does not matter in terms of the Patriots' strength of schedule, but a Denver win would put both teams at 1-1 as opposed to one pulling away in the AFC playoff race. Sure, New England has to beat them both this year, but the rivals cannibalizing wins against one another is still the preferred outcome. | CBS

Las Vegas Raiders (1-0) at Los Angeles Chargers (0-1): Go Chargers! Both teams are on the Patriots' schedule, so we are going with the one with the worse record. The Raiders might ultimately turn out to be the worse team this season, but until there is actual proof of that we are playing it safe. | CBS

Seattle Seahawks (1-0) at Arizona Cardinals (1-0): Go Seahawks! This pick is solely made with the Patriots' strength of schedule tiebreaker in mind. | FOX

Washington Commanders (0-1) at Dallas Cowboys (0-1): Go good game! Neither team has any direct ties to the Patriots, meaning that the result matters only marginally at this stage in the season. | FOX

Miami Dolphins (0-1) at San Francisco 49ers (1-0): Go 49ers! Once again, we are picking the NFC team over the Patriots' division rival. | FOX

Indianapolis Colts (0-1) at Kansas City Chiefs (1-0): Go Colts! The Chiefs are on the Patriots' schedule, but as mentioned above the preferred outcome is their AFC rivals taking wins off of one another. | NBC

New York Giants (1-0) at Los Angeles Rams (0-1): Go good game! Neither the Giants nor the Rams have any direct ties to the Patriots' fortunes this year or in the 2027 draft, so there is no use in picking one over the other in this game. | ESPN/ABC

articles.title: Lions vs Bills: What happened to Ed Oliver?
articles.summary: Ed Oliver suffered a hip injury during Buffalo Bills warm-ups and was ruled out against the Detroit Lions before their Week 2 matchup.
articles.body:
The Buffalo Bills entered Thursday night's matchup against the Detroit Lions with their defense facing a major test. Buffalo opened the 2026 NFL season with a win over the Houston Texans and was preparing for another difficult matchup in Week 2.

The Bills had largely avoided major injury concerns heading into the game. Wednesday's injury report listed Cole Bishop and Ty Johnson, while Terrel Bernard did not carry an injury designation after being limited in practice.

That left Buffalo with a relatively settled defensive lineup heading into its Week 2 game. However, the team's injury fortune changed shortly before kickoff when one of the team's key defensive linemen suffered an unexpected injury.

Ed Oliver suffers hip injury during Bills warm-ups

Buffalo Bills defensive tackle Ed Oliver Mandatory Credit: Gregory Fisher-USA TODAY Sports

Ed Oliver was ruled out of the Bills' matchup against the Lions. The veteran defensive tackle was not carrying an injury designation entering the game.

ESPN's Adam Schefter reported that Ed Oliver suffered a hip injury during warm-ups before the Bills ruled him out of Thursday night's game against the Lions.

The Bills later confirmed the injury, listing Oliver as inactive in their final injury report. As of this writing, the team has not provided a timetable for his return.

Oliver's absence also leaves Buffalo without one of its established interior defensive linemen for a matchup against a Lions offense that entered Week 2 at 1-0. Detroit rushed for 165 yards against the New Orleans Saints on Sunday, and could pose a threat on the ground against a depleted Buffalo defense. The Bills will have to adjust their defensive-line rotation without Oliver and will hope to mark their first game at the Highmark Stadium with a win.

articles.title: Celtic are 'little bit broken' - but is change of shape 'worth risking'?
articles.summary: After last Sunday's drubbing at Ibrox, Celtic needed a reaction against Ferencvaros in the Europa League.  The concessions were alarming easy from a Celtic p...
articles.body:
After last Sunday's drubbing at Ibrox , Celtic needed a reaction against Ferencvaros in the Europa League. What they got was another timid defeat as the Hungarian outfit secured a deserved 3-1 win.

The concessions were alarming easy from a Celtic perspective and after a lively start, they retreated into their shells.

Empty seats and boos met the final whistle and things don't get any easier for Martin O'Neill's side. They host Rangers in the Scottish Premiership on Sunday.

"It's a little bit broken, a little bit nervy, but we have to fight our way through this," captain Callum McGregor said.

"The only way through it is hard work. It's a tough period. You can see how quickly it comes down on top of you. It's a relatively new group, so we have to learn. You don't get much leeway.

"The ultimate test at the weekend is that we have to win the game. It's about staying together, putting one foot in front of another and we just need another bit of luck."

Ferencvaros' opener came as Bamidele Yusuf was allowed to cut inside from the right flank and his cross-cum-shot deflected into the far corner off Liam Scales .

Celtic drew level through Mika Baur 's tidy finish, but seconds before half-time, the visitors hit the front again.

They won possession back in the Celtic half, Yusuf twisted Kieran Tierney inside-out before squaring to Kristoffer Zachariassen , who cleverly flicked past Viljami Sinisalo despite being closely marked by both Scales and Cameron Carter-Vickers .

Former Celtic captain and manager Neil Lennon called it a "comedy of errors".

In an attempt to wrestle back momentum, O'Neill threw on club-record signing Kasper Hogh at half-time and switched to a 4-4-2 system, but it was a forgotten former Celtic man who delivered a telling blow soon after.

Daniel Arzani made just two appearances during his time in Glasgow, picking up a severe knee injury on his debut. One pass from Yusuf opened Celtic up and Arzani cut inside Carter-Vickers before unleashing a fine strike into the far top corner.

At no stage did it look like Celtic would get back in the game and Ferencvaros managed the remainder of the game to take all three points.

"Tonight was I think a European lesson for us in many aspects," O'Neill said. "We'll get ourselves together. We need to re-energise ourselves as much as anything else.

"When we have decent possession of the ball, just don't give it away. But also I think taking a few risks as well too - risks in the proper areas of the field."

Every time there was a backwards pass, groans rang out from the Celtic Park stands. Too often simple passes went astray and forward balls failed to stick.

O'Neill's tactics and team selection were questioned after the weekend. He responded defensively pre-match when asked about the four changes he made on Thursday, including a return in goal for Sinisalo.

That spiky interview with TNT Sports was perhaps indicative of the pressure he is now under, but Petrov - who played under O'Neill for five years - does not recognise his former manager's influence on this team.

"It's not Martin O'Neill's style," Petrov said. "It's too slow at the moment. If you ask me honestly if that's the style Martin O'Neill plays, definitely not.

"When you have your centre-backs making more passes than your midfielders, you can't dominate. Celtic were playing safe. When did Celtic start playing with fear?"

Duran had just eight touches in the first half. Hogh huffed and puffed for little reward in the second. Both also struggled to get into the game against Rangers.

"Kasper Hogh, he's 100 miles an hour. Sometimes you need to relax and have a clear mind," Petrov added. "He tried to do everything. Celtic are rushing everything."

O'Neill hinted his second-half change of shape - going to a midfielder four with two strikers - might also be something he employs on Sunday as he searches for a fix and a way of getting both Duran and Hogh in their favoured positions.

"The club has been used to 4-3-3 for quite some considerable time for quite a number of years as well," he said. "If we're going to get the best out of our best players then we're gong to have to find another way.

"We went 4-4-2 in the second half. That deprives you for the extra player in the middle of the field but it was worth risking."

Alexander : The club needs a full overhaul, very disappointing results.

Mark : O'Neill, Maloney and Fotheringham's record in our past three big ties? P-3, W-0, L-3, F-2, A-11. Time to go. We need a REAL management team - not clueless stooges for the board!

Neil : Celtic should double Neil Lennon's salary and get him in to coach this team and tighten them up.

Mark : Very disappointing night. No desire shown. I'm dreading Sunday!

Jim : McGregor is done no legs negative passing every ball

Danny : Disappointing loss tonight, again. There seems to be a mentality problem with the team. We look hesitant, shaky and inexperienced, constantly getting outclassed by opponents with sides no better than our own. Celtic Park used to be a place that teams feared, now European teams must be licking their lips seeing us in their fixtures. Onto Sunday we go :/

articles.title: Everything Texans STC Frank Ross said ahead of Week 2's matchup vs. Bengals
articles.summary: Here's everything Houston Texans special teams coordinator Frakn Ross said Thursday ahead of Week 2's matchup against the Cincinnati Bengals, including his t...
articles.body:
Here's everything Houston Texans special teams coordinator Frakn Ross said Thursday ahead of Week 2's matchup against the Cincinnati Bengals , including his thoughts on the Bengals ' wide receiver room, preparing for the kick and more.

Frank Ross: "If there's a larger discrepancy in, maybe one of you could research, in experience between me and [ Bengals Special Teams Coordinator] Darrin Simmons, I'd like to know what that split is because he's been a special teams coach for the Bengals for 24 seasons. I have not seen it all but that guy has definitely seen it all and their tape shows it. We have to make sure we match their level of discipline. What Cincinnati is very good at is, they spread the field tremendously with their coverage units. They eliminate really good players by doing that. They play really sound football. It's impressive because that's been on repeat. Otherwise, you're not around for 24 years. That's what's so impressive about Coach Simmons, a lot of respect for them. Then from a specialist standpoint, they have a really good kicker [K Evan McPherson ]. The punter, Ryan] Rehkow, has set the franchise record for longest punts and gross average. This guy has a hammer. For us, we have to make sure, can we find a way to affect that and get some yards, starting our field position in a better spot than a week ago. We have to find a way to get a win. I'm excited for the opportunity to get this Sunday kickoff going."

Q : On the special teams performance in Week 1 and WR Jaylin Noel as a returner

Ross: "First, I'll start with what I liked. Just like anything else, you need to finish strong. Look at how we played when it mattered the most in the kind of final moments in that fourth quarter of the game. We were at our best. That's how you finish. I was super proud of that. It's Week 1, like anything, you have to get the feel. You have to get that out a little bit. Not an excuse, but we need to play better and start fast this week. That goes without saying. To your point, Jaylin Noel, I love this kid. No one's going to convince me otherwise. Make some better decisions. He knows that. He's a very smart football player. I love his intelligence. Love the playmaker in him. Trust him with everything, with the Texans to go and handle the football. Then of course, you don't necessarily expect the ball to bounce and roll 24 yards after a mishit punt. But we always say, 'Do everything you can to field that out of the air.' Just improve that decision-making and try and eliminate something going from bad to worse as best we can. Those outcomes sometimes happen. You have to shake those off and get back to the next play."

Q: On what can be done to better defend returns

Ross: "When you talk to any of our guys, I'm sure you've asked and they say, kickoff and coverage, that's special teams, that's effort. I don't question our effort. We have to get better block destruction quicker and stay clean, meaning uncovered. We had a great end of half kickoff, burned time, then they only have one play on offense and then bang, the half's over. We get a blatant hold call, but the ball gets out. We're not allowed to get held. Our rule is, you better break his arms off because you're not allowed to get held. So as an example, they're holding leverage on the ball and making sure we tackle the runner. Playing with cleaner blocks, instant block shed, block defeat and destruction will be better for us this week."

Q: On how to judge when to call for a fair catch or to return a punt

Ross: "[Jaylin Noel] is an aggressive returner. He wants, as soon as he caught that ball and waved it off, he knew that he wanted that one back. When you have that, first off, it's an instinctual runner, that feeling of knowing when you're getting compression down. He just had a little bit of a want and a redo. We don't get those redo's. It's our chance this Sunday to take any field punt we get when we're in a return call and get that thing started. He'll be just fine, I promise you that."

Q: On whether he has shown the clip of Commanders S Tyler Owens' effort on special teams to the team

Ross: "I have not gone to that. We'll get to the NFL clips usually. I do my around the league on Saturdays and show that, but impressive. I love that effort and I love that it's getting covered by the NFL from special teams because that kid is an animal. Let's find the Texans that do that this Sunday."

articles.title: New Details Emerge on Workout That Left NHL Prospect with ‘Zero Chance of Recovery’: Reports
articles.summary: Four teammates reportedly carried Mayich to shade after he collapsed on Aug. 20
articles.body:
Two new reports provide details about the workout that left NHL prospect Matthew Mayich in the hospital

Mayich was reportedly "disoriented" during the bear crawl portion of the workout and collapsed during the final exercise

The 21-year-old has "zero chance of recovery," his attorney said earlier this month

NHL prospect Matthew Mayich struggled to stand multiple times before collapsing during the military-style workout with the Arizona State Sun Devils that left him hospitalized, witnesses allege in two new reports.

A report from The Athletic , published Thursday, Sept. 16, provides new details about the workout led by Tim Ziesel, a former Green Beret unaffiliated with Arizona State who was brought in to run a special workout with the hockey team on Aug. 20, their first day of organized practices.

Ziesel, who reportedly had a "handshake agreement" with head coach Greg Powers to lead the Sun Devils' practice according to Arizona Republic reporter Robert Anglen, took the team through different movements, such as squats and push-ups, at Sun Angel Stadium, the university's unshaded track and field facilities.

According to The Athletic, which interviewed 12 people either at the workout or briefed on it, Mayich, 21, appeared "disoriented" while doing bear crawls across the field. The witness told the outlet Mayich appeared to catch himself before he almost collapsed after that exercise.

Two other players on the team vomited during the workout, The Athletic reported.

Ziesel reportedly belittled players during the workout, according to The Athletic, and he left after assigning the final event of the workout — a relay race requiring players to carry a medicine ball.

Mayich was reportedly one of the last players to begin the race, and he collapsed after stumbling and dropping the ball, sources told The Athletic. He reportedly attempted to get up twice before collapsing a final time.

Sources told the outlet that one player and an assistant coach shouted for assistance before teammates "found him lying on the ground, incoherent and distressed, unable to respond to questions."

Follow your favorite athletes on and off the field with PEOPLE's free sports newsletter — sign up now!

Mayich remained in the sun for several minutes after he collapsed. Four of his Sun Devils teammates reportedly then carried him into the shade and an athletic trainer retrieved water and an ice pack to put on his chest, according to The Athletic. An ambulance arrived at the stadium at 8:31 a.m., around an hour and a half after the workout began, the outlet said.

Rob Carey, the attorney representing the Mayich family, told ESPN the sophomore athlete suffered "exertional heat stroke that caused a lack of oxygen to the brain."

"There were no other contributing conditions, only exertion-related heat. This is not an induced coma," Carey told the outlet, adding, "We need a miracle."

Carey told the Arizona Republic on Sept. 1 that Mayich has "zero chance of recovery."

PEOPLE has reached out to Ziesel's attorney for comment.

articles.title: Nico Collins may miss the Texans-Bengals game. How Houston can replace its star receiver
articles.summary: Nico Collins' status is uncertain after a hamstring injury. The Texans have several ways to replace their top receiver against Cincinnati.
articles.body:
When the Houston Texans lost second-year wide receiver Jayden Higgins earlier this summer to an ACL injury , they knew they needed to acquire another starter at wide receiver.

And not just because of what Higgins brought to the team.

Their star receiver, Nico Collins , had also dealt with a series of injuries in his five seasons with the team - most notably in last year's playoff loss to the Patriots. The Texans eventually added more depth and talent.

But that depth and talent will be tested this weekend.

Collins suffered a hamstring injury in practice Wednesday and missed practice entirely Thursday, raising significant doubts about his status for Sunday's noon game against the Cincinnati Bengals .

So what will Houston do in the meantime?

Outside of Collins, the Texans have four other receivers on the 53-man roster: Xavier Hutchinson , Kayshon Boutte , Jaylin Noel and Jared Wayne .

There probably isn't a clear No. 1 option among them, though that may not be a problem. C.J. Stroud often likes to distribute the ball to a variety of receivers. While Collins led the team with seven catches for 75 yards and a touchdown last week, Stroud distributed the ball to 11 different players in the 36-31 loss to Buffalo.

Hutchinson was third in that group with three catches for 32 yards. He has experience stepping up whenever there is an injury among the wide receivers.

"We all prepare like we're receiver No. 1," Hutchinson said when asked whether having experience filling in makes things easier. "You've got to be delusional about yourself and what you can do. And I feel everybody has the right delusion and confidence in themselves.

Then there's Boutte, whom the Texans traded for because they felt he could be the deep-play threat he was in New England . He had just one catch for 21 yards on two targets last week against the Bills, but Stroud seemed confident they could develop success in the future.

"He knows how to get open," Stroud said of Boutte. "I know we didn't connect on a couple of them, but we're still building that chemistry. He knows how to get open and play fast."

Stroud's games without his top option have been a mixed bag since he entered the league. He's had both some of his worst performances and some of his best.

Some of his best performances without Collins include his 2023 game against the Bengals, when he led the team on a game-winning field-goal drive. There was also last year's win over the 49ers, when he passed for 318 yards and two touchdowns.

When Collins hasn't played, Stroud typically spreads the ball around more. In the win over the 49ers last season, Stroud completed passes to 10 different players.

"The good thing about the offense is we have a lot of guys we have trust in," offensive coordinator Nick Caley said. "We go through our reads, and the ball finds the open guy."

But some of Stroud's worst performances have come when Collins has been sidelined, including his four-interception showing in the playoff loss to the Patriots and his 86-yard passing performance in a loss to the Packers in 2024.

He is 5-4 in nine starts without Collins in the lineup. Sunday's game will likely mark his 10th start without his star receiver.

Collins' two best attributes are his ability to make contested catches and generate explosive plays. Stroud had a 125 passer rating when targeting him last week. That's something the Texans will miss. So what's the solution?

The Texans will need to find ways to get Jaylin Noel and Boutte the ball more often. Noel didn't see much time on the field as a rookie. And he ran just 15 routes Sunday, compared with 37 for Collins.

That could be, in part, because Collins is an every-down receiver who plays on the outside, while Noel mostly runs routes from the slot.

Noel had two catches for 53 yards and led all receivers in separation yards. He's good when he gets out in space and has a unique ability to make players miss.

"We were mixing groupings," Caley said when asked why Boutte and Noel didn't get more reps. "I think some weeks you're going to see that, and some weeks I think the flow of the game will dictate some of those things. Whether there are more multiple-tight-end groupings, more 11 personnel with a bunch of different groupings that we can deploy to move those guys around, it switches their identity based on grouping.

"Nothing those guys have done. I've been pleased with the progress of the entire unit."

But getting those two players going doesn't have to be the only solution. The Texans can also lean on their running game, which was a major plus in their game against Buffalo. Running back David Montgomery ran for 60 yards and three touchdowns, while Woody Marks added 42 yards. Those two running backs kept Stroud out of third-and-long situations, which helped him convert manageable third downs. The offense faced third-and-3 on seven of its 18 third downs. The Texans also converted 43.8% of their third downs.

The Texans could also use bigger groupings, such as 12 personnel (two tight ends and two wide receivers) and 13 personnel (one wide receiver and three tight ends). The Texans ran 11 personnel (three receivers and one tight end) on 57.5% of their plays last week, while running both 12 and 13 personnel on 13.7% of their plays.

Whatever the Texans choose to do, they have plenty of options and just a few days to get it right.

"I think having the mindset of being open-minded and being flexible is something that, as an entire staff, we all try to do, and we all support each other in that," Caley said. "Just be ready to adjust when need be and try to put our guys in the best position possible."

articles.body:
The New York Giants started their season in impressive fashion when they defeated the Dallas Cowboys by a 28-20 margin in the season opener. New head coach John Harbaugh has high hopes that his team that includes QB Jaxson Dart , RB Cam Skattebo and WR Malik Nabers has a chance to exceed expectations and play much better football than Giants fans have seen from the their team in recent years.

The Giants will be tested in Week 2 when they face the Los Angeles Rams Monday night at SoFi Stadium. The Rams came into the season as the favorite to win the NFC West title and potentially win the Super Bowl this season. The Rams were beaten decisively in their season opener when they met the division rival San Francisco 49ers in Melbourne, Australia. The Giants will likely face an angry and determined team when the two teams meet at SoFi Stadium.

Nabers is probably the most dangerous weapon the Giants have on their roster. He is coming back from a torn ACL. He was targeted 9 times in the game against the Cowboys and he caught 6 passes for 69 yards. However, Nabers was not thrilled with the way he played in the game and he admitted that his performance was "rusty ."

Nabers said that his propensity for slipping and falling on the field took away from his ability to make plays for the Giants and that he should be able to perform at a higher level in the games that follow. If he can pick up his performance this week, it should give the Giants a better chance to compete against the high-powered Rams.
